path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 907. Certification of records to court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 907. Certification of records to court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 907. Certification of records to court (2023)
content:
Whenever a caveat shall be filed or a dispute shall arise before the register concerning
   the probate of a will, the grant of letters or the performance of any other function
   by the register, he may certify, or the court upon petition of any party in interest
   may direct the register at any stage of the proceedings to certify, the entire record
   to the court, which shall proceed to a determination of the issue in dispute.  No letters of administration pendente lite shall be granted by the register after
   proceedings have been removed to the court except by leave of court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 911. Attestation of certain applications and documents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 911. Attestation of certain applications and documents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 911. Attestation of certain applications and documents (2023)
content:
Except as provided otherwise in section 3154 (relating to affidavit and oath), applications
   and documents submitted to the register for which attestation is required may be attested
   either by an affidavit or by a verified statement.  In case of the latter alternative, the statement shall set forth that it is subject
   to the penalties of18 Pa.C.S. § 4904(relating to unsworn falsification to authorities).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 921. Wills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 921. Wills
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 921. Wills (2023)
content:
All probated wills shall be indexed and recorded by the register, and shall remain
   in his office, except for the period required to be in the custody of a higher court.  The recording may be accomplished by photographic or other mechanical process.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 923. Certified copies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 923. Certified copies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 923. Certified copies (2023)
content:
Every register upon the request of any person paying the fee therefor, shall make
   and certify under the seal of his office true copies of his records or of papers filed
   with him or of proceedings before him.  Such certified copies shall be as good evidence as the original in any judicial
   proceeding in the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 908. Appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction and Powers › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 908. Appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 908. Appeals (2023)
content:
(a) When allowed.--Any party in interest seeking to challenge the probate of a will or who is otherwise
      aggrieved by a decree of the register, or a fiduciary whose estate or trust is so
      aggrieved, may appeal therefrom to the court within one year of the decree:  Provided,
      That the executor designated in an instrument shall not by virtue of such designation
      be deemed a party in interest who may appeal from a decree refusing probate of it.  The court, upon petition of a party in interest, may limit the time for appeal to
      three months.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 925. Certificates and affidavits of death
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 925. Certificates and affidavits of death
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 925. Certificates and affidavits of death (2023)
content:
Where it is not necessary to have letters granted to administer a decedent's estate
   but it is desired to have a public record of his death, a certificate of death may
   be filed with the register except that where a certificate of death cannot be obtained
   the affidavit of a relative or other interested party may be filed with the register
   setting forth the decedent's name, residence, date, time and place of death, and age
   at death.  The register shall index and record all such certificates and affidavits filed with
   him.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 922. Inventories
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 922. Inventories
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 922. Inventories (2023)
content: The register shall index and record all inventories filed with him.  The recording may be accomplished by photographic or other mechanical process.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2102. Share of surviving spouse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2102. Share of surviving spouse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2102. Share of surviving spouse (2023)
content: The intestate share of a decedent's surviving spouse is:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2106. Forfeiture
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2106. Forfeiture
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2106. Forfeiture (2023)
content: (a) Spouse's share.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Intestate estate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Intestate estate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Intestate estate (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--All or any part of the estate of a decedent not effectively disposed of by will or
      otherwise passes to his heirs as prescribed in this chapter, except as modified by
      the decedent's will.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2103. Shares of others than surviving spouse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2103. Shares of others than surviving spouse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2103. Shares of others than surviving spouse (2023)
content:
The share of the estate, if any, to which the surviving spouse is not entitled, and
   the entire estate if there is no surviving spouse, shall pass in the following order:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2104. Rules of succession
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2104. Rules of succession
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2104. Rules of succession (2023)
content:
The provisions of this chapter shall be applied to both real and personal estate in
   accordance with the following rules:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2105. Spouse's rights
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2105. Spouse's rights
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2105. Spouse's rights (2023)
content:
(a) Widow.--The share of the estate to which a widow is entitled under this title shall be in
      lieu and full satisfaction of her dower at common law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2109.1. Advancements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2109.1. Advancements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2109.1. Advancements (2023)
content:
If a person dies intestate as to all or any part of his estate, property which he
   gave in his lifetime to an heir is treated as an advancement against the latter's
   share of the estate only if declared in a writing by the decedent or acknowledged
   in writing by the heir to be an advancement.  For this purpose the property advanced is valued as of the time the heir came into
   possession or enjoyment of the property or as of the time of death of the decedent,
   whichever first occurs.  If the recipient of the property fails to survive the decedent, the property is
   not taken into account in computing the intestate share to be received by the recipient's
   issue unless the declaration or acknowledgment so provides.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2110. Spouse's allowance; procedure
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2110. Spouse's allowance; procedure
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2110. Spouse's allowance; procedure (2023)
content:
The allowance shall be set aside and awarded in distribution to the surviving spouse,
   or his successor in interest, in the same manner as other distributive shares of the
   estate are awarded, without any right in the surviving spouse to choose particular
   real or personal property in satisfaction thereof.  Nothing herein shall be construed as limiting the right of the surviving spouse
   and other distributees to demand that property, not theretofore sold, be distributed
   in kind to them.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 9. Register of Wills›Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 924. Recording proceedings in another county
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 9. Register of Wills › Subchapter B. Records and Certified Copies › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 924. Recording proceedings in another county
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 924. Recording proceedings in another county (2023)
content:
Copies of wills and probate proceedings and records of the grant of letters of administration
   and proceedings relating thereto, duly certified by the register, may be filed in
   the office of the register in any county where real estate of the decedent is located.  The register with whom such papers are filed shall forthwith record the same, and
   the record thereof shall be as valid and effectual in law as the original, or its
   duly certified copy, or its record would be for all purposes of vesting title, of
   evidence, and of notice.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2203. Right of election; resident decedent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2203. Right of election; resident decedent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2203. Right of election; resident decedent (2023)
content:
(a) Property subject to election.--Except as provided in subsection (c), when a married person domiciled in this Commonwealth
      dies, his surviving spouse has a right to an elective share of one-third of the following
      property:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2205. Transfers for value excluded
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2205. Transfers for value excluded
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2205. Transfers for value excluded (2023)
content:
Conveyances and contracts made by the decedent are excluded from the provisions of
   section 2203 (relating to right of election;  resident decedent) and section 2204
   (relating to disclaimers, releases and charges against elective share), to the extent
   that the decedent received adequate consideration therefor in money or money's worth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2204. Disclaimers, releases and charges against elective share
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2204. Disclaimers, releases and charges against elective share
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2204. Disclaimers, releases and charges against elective share (2023)
content:
(a) Disclaimers.--Except as provided in subsections (b) and (c), an election by a spouse to take his
      elective share shall be deemed a disclaimer of any beneficial interest of the spouse
      in the following, to the extent that such interest would otherwise be payable to or
      enjoyed by the spouse after the decedent's death:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2201. Definition of conveyance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2201. Definition of conveyance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2201. Definition of conveyance (2023)
content:
As used in this chapter, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise, “conveyance” means an act by which it is intended to create an interest in real or personal property
   whether the act is intended to have inter vivos or testamentary operation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2206. Right of election personal to surviving spouse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2206. Right of election personal to surviving spouse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2206. Right of election personal to surviving spouse (2023)
content:
The right of election of the surviving spouse may be exercised in whole or in part
   only during his lifetime by him or by his agent in accordance with section 5603(d)
   (relating to implementation of power of attorney).  In the case of a minor spouse, the right of election may be exercised in whole or
   in part only by the spouse's guardian;  in the case of an incapacitated spouse, the
   right of election may be exercised in whole or in part only by the spouse's guardian
   or by his agent in accordance with section 5603(d) if the power of attorney qualifies
   as a durable power of attorney under section 5604 (relating to durable powers of attorney);
   provided, that, in each case, the election shall be exercised only upon order of the
   court having jurisdiction of the minor's or the incapacitated person's estate, after
   finding that exercise of the right is advisable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2208. Forfeiture of right of election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2208. Forfeiture of right of election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2208. Forfeiture of right of election (2023)
content:
A surviving spouse who under the provisions of section 2106 (relating to forfeiture)
   would not be entitled to a share of the decedent's estate had he died intestate shall
   have no right of election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2207. Waiver of right to elect
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2207. Waiver of right to elect
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2207. Waiver of right to elect (2023)
content:
The right of election of a surviving spouse may be waived, wholly or partially, before
   or after marriage or before or after the death of the decedent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2107. Persons born out of wedlock
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2107. Persons born out of wedlock
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2107. Persons born out of wedlock (2023)
content:
(a) Child of mother.--For purposes of descent by, from and through a person born out of wedlock, he shall
      be considered the child of his mother.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Who may make a will
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Who may make a will
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Who may make a will (2023)
content: Any person 18 or more years of age who is of sound mind may make a will.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 21. Intestate Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2108. Adopted person
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 21. Intestate Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2108. Adopted person
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2108. Adopted person (2023)
content:
For purposes of inheritance by, from and through an adopted person he shall be considered
   the issue of his adopting parent or parents.  An adopted person shall not be considered as continuing to be the child or issue
   of his natural parents except in distributing the estate of a natural kin, other than
   the natural parent, who has maintained a family relationship with the adopted person.  If a natural parent shall have married the adopting parent, the adopted person for
   purposes of inheritance by, from and through him shall also be considered the issue
   of such natural parent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2209. Surviving spouse as witness
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2209. Surviving spouse as witness
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2209. Surviving spouse as witness (2023)
content:
A person who is or claims to be the surviving spouse shall be a competent witness
   as to all matters pertinent to his rights under this chapter other than the creation
   of his status as the surviving spouse.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Revocation of a will
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Revocation of a will
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Revocation of a will (2023)
content:
No will or codicil in writing, or any part thereof, can be revoked or altered otherwise
   than:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2202. Right of election; nonresident decedent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2202. Right of election; nonresident decedent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2202. Right of election; nonresident decedent (2023)
content:
When a married person not domiciled in this Commonwealth dies, the rights, if any,
   of his surviving spouse to an elective share in property in this Commonwealth are
   governed by the laws of the decedent's domicile at death, but the rights of the electing
   spouse shall be subject to the rights of fiduciaries, custodians and obligors within
   this Commonwealth and transferees for value of and holders of liens for value on real
   estate or tangible personal property located in this Commonwealth under section 2211
   (relating to determination of effect of election;  enforcement).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2210. Procedure for election; time limit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2210. Procedure for election; time limit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2210. Procedure for election; time limit (2023)
content:
(a) How election made.--A surviving spouse's election to take or not to take his elective share shall be
      by a writing signed by him and filed with the clerk of the orphans' court division
      of the county where the decedent died domiciled.  Notice of the election shall be given to the decedent's personal representative,
      if any.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Form and execution of a will
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Form and execution of a will
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Form and execution of a will (2023)
content:
Every will shall be in writing and shall be signed by the testator at the end thereof,
   subject to the following rules and exceptions:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2211. Determination of effect of election; enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 22. Elective Share of Surviving Spouse › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2211. Determination of effect of election; enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2211. Determination of effect of election; enforcement (2023)
content:
(a) Power of court of domicile.--After notice and hearing, the orphans' court division of the county of the decedent's
      domicile shall determine all matters concerning the spouse's election, including the
      interests and liabilities of the spouse and others in or with respect to all property,
      regardless of its situs, which is subject to the election or which must be disclaimed,
      released or conveyed by the spouse or charged against the elective share.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. Rules of interpretation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. Rules of interpretation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. Rules of interpretation (2023)
content:
In the absence of a contrary intent appearing therein, wills shall be construed as
   to real and personal estate in accordance with the following rules:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504.1. Validity of execution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504.1. Validity of execution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504.1. Validity of execution (2023)
content:
A will is validly executed if executed in compliance with section 2502 (relating to
   form and execution of a will), or in compliance with the law of the jurisdiction where
   the testator was domiciled at the time of the execution of the will or at the time
   of his death.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Revival of revoked or invalid will
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Revival of revoked or invalid will
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Revival of revoked or invalid will (2023)
content:
If, after the making of any will, the testator shall execute a later will which expressly
   or by necessary implication revokes the earlier will, the revocation of the later
   will shall not revive the earlier will, unless the revocation is in writing and declares
   the intention of the testator to revive the earlier will, or unless, after such revocation,
   the earlier will shall be reexecuted.  Oral republication of itself shall be ineffective to revive a will.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2507. Modification by circumstances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2507. Modification by circumstances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2507. Modification by circumstances (2023)
content:
Wills shall be modified upon the occurrence of any of the following circumstances,
   among others:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2515. Devise or bequest to trust
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2515. Devise or bequest to trust
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2515. Devise or bequest to trust (2023)
content:
A devise or bequest in a will may be made to the trustee of a trust, including any
   unfunded trust, established in writing by the testator or any other person before,
   concurrently with or after the execution of the will.  Such devise or bequest shall not be invalid because the trust is amendable or revocable,
   or both, or because the trust was amended after execution of the will.  Unless the will provides otherwise, the property so devised or bequeathed shall
   not be deemed held under a testamentary trust of the testator but shall become and
   be a part of the principal of the trust to which it is given to be administered and
   disposed of in accordance with the provisions of the instrument establishing that
   trust and any amendment thereof.  An entire revocation of the trust prior to the testator's death shall invalidate
   the devise or bequest unless the will directs otherwise.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 28. Formula Clauses for Federal Tax Purposes›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2802. Interpretation of formula clauses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 28. Formula Clauses for Federal Tax Purposes › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2802. Interpretation of formula clauses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2802. Interpretation of formula clauses (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (b) and subject to section 2803 (relating to judicial
      proceeding), a will, trust or other dispositive instrument of a decedent who dies
      after December 31, 2009, and before January 1, 2011, that contains a formula clause
      shall be rebuttably presumed to be interpreted pursuant to the Federal estate tax
      and generation-skipping transfer tax laws applicable to estates of decedents dying
      on December 31, 2009.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2516. Devise in fee tail abolished
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2516. Devise in fee tail abolished
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2516. Devise in fee tail abolished (2023)
content:
Whenever by any devise an estate in fee tail would be created according to the common
   law of the Commonwealth, it shall pass an estate in fee simple, and as such shall
   be inheritable and freely alienable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 27. Contractual Arrangements Relating to Succession›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2701. Contracts concerning succession
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 27. Contractual Arrangements Relating to Succession › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2701. Contracts concerning succession
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2701. Contracts concerning succession (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment of contract.--A contract to die intestate or to make or not to revoke a will or testamentary provision
      or an obligation dischargeable only at or after death can be established in support
      of a claim against the estate of a decedent only by:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2518. Alienage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2518. Alienage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2518. Alienage (2023)
content:
Real and personal estate shall pass without regard to whether the testator or any
   devisee or legatee is or has been an alien.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 28. Formula Clauses for Federal Tax Purposes›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2803. Judicial proceeding
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 28. Formula Clauses for Federal Tax Purposes › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2803. Judicial proceeding
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2803. Judicial proceeding (2023)
content:
(a) Standing.--The decedent's personal representative, trustee or any affected beneficiary under
      the will, trust or other dispositive instrument may bring a proceeding to interpret
      a formula clause.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 28. Formula Clauses for Federal Tax Purposes›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2801. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 28. Formula Clauses for Federal Tax Purposes › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2801. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2801. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2521. Penalty clause for contest
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2521. Penalty clause for contest
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2521. Penalty clause for contest (2023)
content:
A provision in a will or trust purporting to penalize an interested person for contesting
   the will or trust or instituting other proceedings relating to the estate or trust
   is unenforceable if probable cause exists for instituting proceedings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2517. Rule in Shelley's case and doctrine of worthier title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2517. Rule in Shelley's case and doctrine of worthier title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2517. Rule in Shelley's case and doctrine of worthier title (2023)
content:
(a) Rule in Shelley's case.--The rule in Shelley's case and its corollaries shall not be applied, and a devise
      or bequest directly or in trust which shall express an intent to create an estate
      for life with remainder to the life tenant's heirs or the heirs of his body or his
      issue or his next of kin or persons described by words of similar import shall not
      operate to give such life tenant an estate in fee in real estate or an absolute estate
      in personalty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter B. Family Exemption›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3122. Payment or delivery of exemption
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter B. Family Exemption › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3122. Payment or delivery of exemption
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3122. Payment or delivery of exemption (2023)
content:
(a) Items claimed.--The personal representative, if any, shall deliver to the spouse, child or children,
      parent or parents, the items of personal property claimed as the exemption, at the
      values fixed by the inventory and appraisement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter B. Family Exemption›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3121. When allowable
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter B. Family Exemption › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3121. When allowable
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3121. When allowable (2023)
content:
The spouse of any decedent dying domiciled in the Commonwealth, and if there be no
   spouse, or if he has forfeited his rights, then such children as are members of the
   same household as the decedent, and in the event there are no such children, then
   the parent or parents of the decedent who are members of the same household as the
   decedent, may retain or claim as an exemption either real or personal property, or
   both, not theretofore sold by the personal representative, to the value of $3,500:
   Provided, That property specifically devised or bequeathed by the decedent, or otherwise
   specifically disposed of by him, may not be so retained or claimed if other assets
   are available for the exemption.  The surviving husband or wife shall be a competent witness as to all matters pertinent
   to the issue of forfeiture of the right to exemption.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter A. Dispositions Independent of Letters›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3102. Settlement of small estates on petition
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter A. Dispositions Independent of Letters › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3102. Settlement of small estates on petition
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3102. Settlement of small estates on petition (2023)
content:
When any person dies domiciled in the Commonwealth owning property (exclusive of real
   estate and of property payable under section 3101 (relating to payments to family
   and funeral directors), but including personal property claimed as the family exemption)
   of a gross value not exceeding $50,000, the orphans' court division of the county
   wherein the decedent was domiciled at the time of his death, upon petition of any
   party in interest, in its discretion, with or without appraisement, and with such
   notice as the court shall direct, and whether or not letters have been issued or a
   will probated, may direct distribution of the property (including property not paid
   under section 3101) to the parties entitled thereto.  The authority of the court to award distribution of personal property under this
   section shall not be restricted because of the decedent's ownership of real estate,
   regardless of its value.  The decree of distribution so made shall constitute sufficient authority to all
   transfer agents, registrars and others dealing with the property of the estate to
   recognize the persons named therein as entitled to receive the property to be distributed
   without administration, and shall in all respects have the same effect as a decree
   of distribution after an accounting by a personal representative.  Within one year after such a decree of distribution has been made, any party in
   interest may file a petition to revoke it because an improper distribution has been
   ordered.  If the court shall find that an improper distribution has been ordered, it shall
   revoke the decree and shall direct restitution as equity and justice shall require.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter A. Dispositions Independent of Letters›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3101. Payments to family and funeral directors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter A. Dispositions Independent of Letters › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3101. Payments to family and funeral directors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3101. Payments to family and funeral directors (2023)
content:
(a) Wages, salary or employee benefits.--Any employer of a person dying domiciled in this Commonwealth at any time after the
      death of the employee, whether or not a personal representative has been appointed,
      may pay wages, salary or any employee benefits due the deceased in an amount not exceeding
      $10,000 to the spouse, any child, the father or mother, or any sister or brother (preference
      being given in the order named) of the deceased employee.  Any employer making such a payment shall be released to the same extent as if payment
      had been made to a duly appointed personal representative of the decedent and he shall
      not be required to see to the application thereof.  Any person to whom payment is made shall be answerable therefor to anyone prejudiced
      by an improper distribution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter B. Family Exemption›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3126. Grantee or lienholder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter B. Family Exemption › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3126. Grantee or lienholder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3126. Grantee or lienholder (2023)
content:
(a) Rights accruing before death;  purchase money obligation.--Nothing in Subchapter A of this chapter1(relating to dispositions independent of letters) and this subchapter shall be construed
      as impairing any lien existing at death for the purchase money of real estate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter B. Family Exemption›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3123. Payment from real estate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter B. Family Exemption › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3123. Payment from real estate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3123. Payment from real estate (2023)
content:
(a) Appraisement.--If the exemption is claimed in whole or in part out of real estate, the appraisement
      of the real estate shall be made by two appraisers appointed by the court, upon petition
      and after such notice as the court shall direct.  The orphans' court division of the county where letters testamentary or of administration
      have been granted, or should no letters have been granted then of the county within
      which was the family or principal residence of the decedent, shall have jurisdiction
      concerning the exemption, whether the real estate is situate in that county or in
      any other county of the Commonwealth.  When real estate is located outside of the county of original jurisdiction, the
      orphans' court division of the county of original jurisdiction may, in its discretion,
      direct that an application for the appointment of appraisers shall be made to the
      orphans' court division of the county in which the real estate is located.  The appraisers so appointed shall fix the value of the real estate as of the date
      of presenting the petition for their appointment and shall receive such compensation
      as shall be allowed by the court appointing them.  Exceptions to appraisements shall be filed with the court of original jurisdiction
      which may, in its discretion, refer the exceptions to the orphans' court division
      of the county in which the real estate is located.  Upon compliance with such requirements of notice as the court shall direct, the
      court of original jurisdiction may confirm the appraisement and set apart the real
      estate to the surviving spouse, child or children, parent or parents entitled thereto.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter B. Family Exemption›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3124. Income
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter B. Family Exemption › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3124. Income
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3124. Income (2023)
content:
When the family exemption does not exhaust the entire real and personal estate, the
   income of the estate shall be equitably prorated among the surviving spouse, child
   or children, parent or parents and the others taking the estate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 25. Wills›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2519. Testamentary guardian
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 25. Wills › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2519. Testamentary guardian
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 2519. Testamentary guardian (2023)
content:
(a) Guardian of the person.--A person competent to make a will, being the sole surviving parent or adopting parent
      of any unmarried minor child, may appoint a testamentary guardian of the person of
      such child during his minority, or for any shorter period except that no parent who,
      for one year or upwards previous to his death, shall have willfully neglected or refused
      to provide for his child, or who, for a like period, shall have deserted the child
      or willfully failed to perform parental duties, shall have the right to appoint a
      testamentary guardian of the person of such child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter C. Probate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3131. Place of probate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter C. Probate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3131. Place of probate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3131. Place of probate (2023)
content:
The will of a decedent domiciled in the Commonwealth at the time of his death shall
   be probated only before the register of the county where the decedent had his last
   family or principal residence.  If the decedent had no domicile in the Commonwealth, his will may be probated before
   the register of any county where any of his property is located.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter C. Probate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3133. Limit of time for probate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter C. Probate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3133. Limit of time for probate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3133. Limit of time for probate (2023)
content: (a) Original probate.--A will may be offered for probate at any time.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter C. Probate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3135. Wills in foreign language
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter C. Probate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3135. Wills in foreign language
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3135. Wills in foreign language (2023)
content:
A writing not in English shall not be filed for probate or for any other purpose in
   the office of the register unless there is attached to it and filed with it a translation
   into English, sworn to be correct.  The register shall attach the translation to the original and shall file them in
   his office, and in all cases where a recording is now or hereafter may be required,
   both the original and the translation shall be recorded.  A writing filed in violation of this section shall not constitute notice to any
   person.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter C. Probate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3136. Wills probated outside the Commonwealth
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter C. Probate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3136. Wills probated outside the Commonwealth
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3136. Wills probated outside the Commonwealth (2023)
content:
A duly authenticated copy of a will proved outside of the Commonwealth according to
   the law of the place of probate may be offered for probate before any register having
   jurisdiction, and letters testamentary or of administration with a will annexed may
   be granted thereon as though the original will had been offered before such register.  If, in addition to such copy, there shall be produced a duly authenticated copy
   of the record of the probate proceeding of the original instrument, the will shall
   be entitled to probate in this Commonwealth and appropriate letters shall be issued
   thereon without the production or examination of the witnesses to prove such will,
   unless the will was probated outside of the United States and the record shows or
   it is satisfactorily proved that an essential requirement of Pennsylvania law for
   a valid will has not been met.  If the will was probated outside of the United States, the probate proceedings may
   be supplemented by the submission of additional evidence to the register.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter B. Family Exemption›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3125. Other remedies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter B. Family Exemption › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3125. Other remedies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3125. Other remedies (2023)
content:
The surviving spouse, child or children, parent or parents may also collect the exemption
   out of real and personal estate, together with income thereon, in the manner provided
   by law for the collection of legacies.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter C. Probate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3137. Enforcing production of will
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter C. Probate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3137. Enforcing production of will
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3137. Enforcing production of will (2023)
content:
The register, at the request of any party in interest, shall issue a citation directed
   to any person alleged to have possession or control of a will of a decedent requiring
   him to show cause why it should not be deposited with him.  In the absence of good cause shown, the register shall order the will to be deposited
   with him.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter C. Probate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3132.1. Self-proved wills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter C. Probate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3132.1. Self-proved wills
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3132.1. Self-proved wills (2023)
content:
(a) Proof.--Unless there is a contest with respect to the validity of the will, or unless the
      will is signed by mark or by another as provided in section 2502 (relating to form
      and execution of a will), an affidavit of witness made in conformity with this section
      shall be accepted by the register as proof of the facts stated as if it had been made
      under oath before the register at the time of probate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter D. Grant of Letters›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3151. Proper county
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter D. Grant of Letters › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3151. Proper county
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3151. Proper county (2023)
content:
Letters testamentary or of administration on the estate of a decedent domiciled in
   the Commonwealth at the time of his death shall be granted only by the register of
   the county where the decedent had his last family or principal residence.  If the decedent had no such domicile in the Commonwealth, letters testamentary or
   of administration may be granted by the register of any county wherein property of
   the estate shall be located and, when granted, shall be exclusive throughout the Commonwealth.  If the decedent had no such domicile in the Commonwealth, and had no property located
   therein, and service of process is to be made in the Commonwealth upon his personal
   representative as authorized by law, then letters testamentary or of administration
   on his estate may be granted by the register of any county of the Commonwealth and,
   when granted, shall be exclusive throughout the Commonwealth.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3157. Nonresidents (2023)
content:
The register shall have discretion to refuse letters of administration to any individual
   not a resident of this Commonwealth.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3152. When 21 years elapsed (2023)
content:
Letters testamentary or of administration shall not be granted after the expiration
   of 21 years from the decedent's death, except on the order of the court, upon cause
   shown.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3155. Persons entitled (2023)
content:
(a) Letters testamentary.--Letters testamentary shall be granted by the register to the executor designated in
      the will, whether or not he has declined a trust under the will.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3159. Letters of administration D.B.N. or D.B.N.C.T.A. (2023)
content:
When an entire vacancy occurs in the office of personal representative before administration
   is completed, the register, in a case of intestacy, shall grant letters of administration
   de bonis non, and in the case of testacy, letters de bonis non cum testamento annexo,
   to the person or persons entitled thereto.

All wills shall be proved by the oaths or affirmations of two competent witnesses

(a) Fiduciary and witness.--The affidavit to a petition for the grant of letters and the oath of the fiduciary
      relative to the performance of his duties and, except as provided in subsection (b),

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3160. Letters of administration durante minoritate, durante absentia, and pendente lite (2023)
content:
Whenever the circumstances of the case require, letters of administration durante
   minoritate, durante absentia, or pendente lite may be granted to any fit person or
   persons, after such notice, if any, as the register shall require.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3158. Letters of administration C.T.A. (2023)
content:
When there is a will, but no executor qualifies, letters of administration cum testamento
   annexo may be granted to the person or persons entitled thereto.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter C. Probate›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3138. Later will or codicil
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter C. Probate › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3138. Later will or codicil
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3138. Later will or codicil (2023)
content:
If a later will or codicil is submitted to the register for probate within three months
   of the testator's death but after the register shall have probated an earlier instrument,
   the register, after such notice as he deems advisable, but with at least ten-days'
   notice to the petitioner who presented the probated instrument if he has not requested
   probate of the later will or codicil, shall have power to open the probate record,
   receive proof of the later instrument or instruments and amend his probate record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter D. Grant of Letters›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3163. Submission to jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter D. Grant of Letters › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3163. Submission to jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3163. Submission to jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--By accepting appointment by the register of wills, the personal representative submits
      personally to the jurisdiction of the orphans' court division of the county where
      letters testamentary or letters of administration are granted in all matters involving
      the performance of the personal representative's duties as personal representative,
      and an action by any interested party seeking an accounting by, or removal of, the
      personal representative, or alleging breach of duty by the personal representative,
      shall be commenced by notice to the personal representative.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter E. Personal Representative; Bond›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3172. Register's responsibility

Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter E. Personal Representative; Bond › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3172. Register's responsibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3172. Register's responsibility (2023)
content:
If any register shall grant letters without having taken such bond as is required
   by law, he and his surety shall be liable to pay all damages which shall accrue to
   any person by reason thereof.  Nothing herein stated shall be deemed to relieve the personal representative from
   liability which would otherwise be imposed upon him by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter D. Grant of Letters›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3161. Oath of personal representative
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter D. Grant of Letters › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3161. Oath of personal representative
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3161. Oath of personal representative (2023)
content:
Before letters shall be granted to a personal representative by the register, the
   personal representative shall swear that he will well and truly administer the estate
   according to law.  The oath of a corporate personal representative may be taken by any of its officers.

content:
(a) By the court.--The court, upon cause shown and after such notice, if any, as it shall direct, may
      require a surety bond, or increase or decrease the amount of an existing bond, or
      require more or less security therefor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter E. Personal Representative; Bond›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3173. Fiduciary estate

content:
The register, in his discretion, upon the application of any party in interest, in
   addition to any bond required for the decedent's individual estate, may require a
   separate bond in the name of the Commonwealth, with sufficient surety, in such amount
   as the register shall consider necessary for the protection of the parties in interest
   in an estate of which the decedent was a fiduciary, and conditioned in the following
   form:

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3181. Revocation of letters (2023)
content:
(a) When no will.--The register may revoke letters of administration granted by him whenever it appears
      that the person to whom the letters were granted is not entitled thereto.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter D. Grant of Letters›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3162. Advertisement of grant of letters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter D. Grant of Letters › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3162. Advertisement of grant of letters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3162. Advertisement of grant of letters (2023)
content:
(a) Notice generally.--The personal representative, immediately after the grant of letters, shall cause notice
      thereof to be given in one newspaper of general circulation published at or near the
      place where the decedent resided or, in the case of a nonresident decedent, at or
      near the place where the letters were granted, and in the legal periodical, if any,
      designated by rule of court for the publication of legal notices, once a week for
      three successive weeks, together with his name and address;  and in every such notice,
      he shall request all persons having claims against the estate of the decedent to make
      known the same to him or his attorney, and all persons indebted to the decedent to
      make payment to him without delay.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3183. Procedure for and effect of removal (2023)
content:
The court on its own motion may, and on the petition of any party in interest alleging
   adequate grounds for removal shall, order the personal representative to appear and
   show cause why he should not be removed, or, when necessary to protect the rights
   of creditors or parties in interest, may summarily remove him.  Upon removal, the court may direct the grant of new letters testamentary or of administration
   by the register to the person entitled and may, by summary attachment of the person
   or other appropriate orders, provide for the security and delivery of the assets of
   the estate, together with all books, accounts and papers relating thereto.  Any personal representative summarily removed under the provisions of this section
   may apply, by petition, to have the decree of removal vacated and to be reinstated,
   and, if the court shall vacate the decree of removal and reinstate him, it shall thereupon
   make any orders which may be appropriate to accomplish the reinstatement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter A. Inventory›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3301. Duty of personal representative

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3301. Duty of personal representative (2023)
content:
(a) General assets.--Every personal representative shall file with the register a verified inventory
      of all real and personal estate of the decedent, except real estate outside of this
      Commonwealth.  An ancillary personal representative shall include in the inventory only assets
      for which he is responsible.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3184. Discharge of personal representative and surety (2023)
content:
After confirmation of his final account and distribution to the parties entitled,
   a personal representative and his surety may be discharged by the court from future
   liability.  The court may discharge only the surety from future liability, allowing the personal
   representative to continue without surety, upon condition that no further assets shall
   come into the control of the personal representative until he files another bond with
   sufficient surety, as required by the register.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter E. Personal Representative; Bond›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3171. Individual estate

   representative, and conditioned in the following form:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter A. Inventory›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3304. Claims against personal representative
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter A. Inventory › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3304. Claims against personal representative
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3304. Claims against personal representative (2023)
content:
The appointment of a personal representative shall not operate as a discharge or bequest
   of any debt which he owes the decedent or of any claim which the decedent had against
   him, but any such debt or claim, if it survives, shall be included in the inventory.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter A. Inventory›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3303. Supplemental inventory
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter A. Inventory › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3303. Supplemental inventory
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3303. Supplemental inventory (2023)
content:
Whenever any property not included in the inventory comes to the knowledge of the
   personal representative, he shall file, within 30 days of its discovery, a supplemental
   inventory thereof with the register.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3312. Renunciation of right to administer property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3312. Renunciation of right to administer property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3312. Renunciation of right to administer property (2023)
content:
When any property is of no value to the estate, the court may authorize the personal
   representative to renounce his right to administer it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter A. Inventory›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3302. Valuations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter A. Inventory › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3302. Valuations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3302. Valuations (2023)
content:
The personal representative shall determine and state in figures opposite each item
   of the inventory its fair value as of the date of the decedent's death.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3315. Incorporation of or formation of entity to operate estate's business
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3315. Incorporation of or formation of entity to operate estate's business
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3315. Incorporation of or formation of entity to operate estate's business (2023)
content:
After notice to all parties in interest, aided by the report of a master if necessary,
   and giving due regard to the provisions of the governing instrument and any other
   factor that the court deems relevant, the court may authorize the personal representative
   alone or jointly with others, to organize a corporation, or form a partnership, limited
   liability company or other entity, to carry on the business of the estate, whether
   the business was owned solely or with others, and may contribute for stock of the
   corporation, as capital, or for an interest in a partnership, limited liability company
   or other entity, all or part of the property of the estate which was invested in the
   business.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter A. Inventory›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3305. Objections to inventory
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter A. Inventory › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3305. Objections to inventory
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3305. Objections to inventory (2023)
content:
Objections to the inventory may be made by any party in interest at any time up to
   and including the time fixed by rule of court for making objections to the first account
   of the personal representative.  Such objections in the discretion of the court may be heard at the audit of the
   account.  Objections to the inventory also may be made in the form of objections to the account.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3320. Voting stock by proxy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3320. Voting stock by proxy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3320. Voting stock by proxy (2023)
content:
The personal representatives or a majority of them, either in person or by proxy,
   may vote stock owned by the estate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters›Subchapter E. Personal Representative; Bond›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3174. When not required
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 31. Dispositions Independent of Letters; Family Exemption; Probate of Wills and Grant of Letters › Subchapter E. Personal Representative; Bond › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3174. When not required
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3174. When not required (2023)
content: (a) Corporate personal representative.--No bond shall be required of:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3313. Liability insurance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3313. Liability insurance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3313. Liability insurance (2023)
content:
The personal representative, at the expense of the estate, may protect himself, his
   employees and the beneficiaries by insurance from liability to third persons arising
   from the administration of the estate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316. Investment of funds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316. Investment of funds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316. Investment of funds (2023)
content:
Subject to his duty to liquidate the estate for prompt distribution and to the provisions
   of the will, if any, the personal representative may invest the funds of the estate
   but shall have no duty to do so.  Any such investment, except as the court or the will may otherwise authorize or
   direct, shall be restricted to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3314. Continuation of business
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3314. Continuation of business
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3314. Continuation of business (2023)
content:
Giving due regard to the provisions of the governing instrument and any other factor
   that the court deems relevant, and aided by the report of a master if necessary, the
   court may authorize the personal representative to continue any business of the estate
   for the benefit of the estate.  The order may be with or without notice.  If prior notice is not given to all parties in interest, it shall be given within
   five days after the order or within such extended time as the court, for cause shown,
   shall allow.  Any party in interest may, at any time, petition the court to revoke or modify the
   order.  The order may provide:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316.1. Set-aside
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316.1. Set-aside
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3316.1. Set-aside (2023)
content:
A personal representative may, without court approval, set aside property in a separate
   fund prior to actual distribution, after which income earned on the separate fund
   and appreciation or depreciation of the property set-aside shall belong to the separate
   fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries›Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives›Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities›PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3317. Claims against co-fiduciary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 20 Pa.C.S.A. Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries › Chapter 33. Administration and Personal Representatives › Subchapter B. Personal Representatives; Powers, Duties and Liabilities › PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3317. Claims against co-fiduciary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 20 Pa.C.S.A. § 3317. Claims against co-fiduciary (2023)
content:
When one of two or more personal representatives shall be individually liable to the
