content:
Notwithstanding the provisions of42 Pa.C.S. §§ 3571(relating to Commonwealth portion of fines, etc.) and 3573 (relating to municipal
   corporation portion of fines, etc.), all costs imposed and collected under sections
   3709 (relating to penalties) and 3716 (relating to costs) by a division of the unified
   judicial system existing undersection 1 of Article V of the Constitution of Pennsylvaniaand42 Pa.C.S. § 301(relating to unified judicial system) shall be remitted to the Commonwealth for use
   by the department for administering this chapter.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 13. Marriage License › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1308. Judicial review of refusal to issue license

(a) Certifying proceedings to court.--If the issuance of a marriage license is refused, upon request of the applicants,

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 13. Marriage License › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1303. Waiting period after application

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 11. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Records and statistics

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 13. Marriage License › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1301. Marriage license required

(a) General rule.--The fee to be charged for issuing a marriage license or declaration and for returns
      thereof to the department shall be $3 of which $2.50 shall be retained by the county
      wherein the license is issued and 50¢ shall be remitted to the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 11. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Forms
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 11. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Forms
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Forms (2023)
content:
Marriage license applications, consent certificates, marriage licenses and other necessary
   forms shall be supplied at the expense of the county and shall be uniform throughout
   this Commonwealth as prescribed by the department.  Statements of physicians and laboratories relative to examinations for syphilis
   shall be prepared and furnished by the department.

content:
The marriage license shall not be valid for a longer period than 60 days from the

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 13. Marriage License›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1309. Filing applications and consent certificates
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 13. Marriage License › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1309. Filing applications and consent certificates
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1309. Filing applications and consent certificates (2023)
content:
The applications for marriage licenses and consent certificates shall be immediately
   filed and docketed as public records.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 13. Marriage License›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1302. Application for license
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 13. Marriage License › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1302. Application for license
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1302. Application for license (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No marriage license shall be issued except upon written and verified application made
      by both of the parties intending to marry.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 11. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Short title of part
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 11. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Short title of part
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Short title of part (2023)
content: This part shall be known and may be cited as the Marriage Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 13. Marriage License›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1307. Issuance of license
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 13. Marriage License › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1307. Issuance of license
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1307. Issuance of license (2023)
content:
The marriage license shall be issued if it appears from properly completed applications
   on behalf of each of the parties to the proposed marriage that there is no legal objection
   to the marriage.  Except as provided by section 1303(b) (relating to waiting period after application),
   the license shall not be issued prior to the third day following the date of the most
   recent of the two applications therefor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 15. Marriage Ceremony›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1503. Persons qualified to solemnize marriages

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1503. Persons qualified to solemnize marriages (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The following are authorized to solemnize marriages between persons that produce
      a marriage license issued under this part:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 17. Miscellaneous Provisions Relating to Marriage›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1701. Decree that spouse of applicant is presumed decedent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 17. Miscellaneous Provisions Relating to Marriage › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1701. Decree that spouse of applicant is presumed decedent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1701. Decree that spouse of applicant is presumed decedent (2023)
content:
(a) Finding of death.--When the spouse of an applicant for a marriage license has disappeared or is absent
      from the place of residence of the spouse without being heard of after diligent inquiry,
      the court, aided by the report of a master if necessary, upon petition of the applicant
      for a marriage license, may make a finding and decree that the absentee is dead and
      the date of death if notice to the absentee has been given as provided in subsection
      (d) and either of the applicants is and for one year or more prior to the application
      has been a resident of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part I. General Provisions›Chapter 1. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part I. General Provisions › Chapter 1. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title of title (2023)
content: This title shall be known and may be cited as the Domestic Relations Code.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 15. Marriage Ceremony›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1504. Returns of marriages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 15. Marriage Ceremony › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1504. Returns of marriages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1504. Returns of marriages (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The original marriage certificate shall be signed by the person solemnizing the marriage
      and given to the parties contracting the marriage.  The duplicate certificate shall be signed by the person or by a member of the religious
      society, institution or organization solemnizing the marriage and returned for recording
      within ten days to the court which issued the license.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 17. Miscellaneous Provisions Relating to Marriage›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1703. Marriage within degree of consanguinity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 17. Miscellaneous Provisions Relating to Marriage › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1703. Marriage within degree of consanguinity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1703. Marriage within degree of consanguinity (2023)
content:
All marriages within the prohibited degrees of consanguinity as set forth in this
   part are voidable, but, when any of these marriages have not been dissolved during
   the lifetime of the parties, the unlawfulness of the marriage shall not be inquired
   into after the death of either of the parties to the marriage.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 17. Miscellaneous Provisions Relating to Marriage›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1702. Marriage during existence of former marriage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 17. Miscellaneous Provisions Relating to Marriage › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1702. Marriage during existence of former marriage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1702. Marriage during existence of former marriage (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If a married person, during the lifetime of the other person with whom the marriage
      is in force, enters into a subsequent marriage pursuant to the requirements of this
      part and the parties to the marriage live together thereafter as husband and wife,
      and the subsequent marriage was entered into by one or both of the parties in good
      faith in the full belief that the former spouse was dead or that the former marriage
      has been annulled or terminated by a divorce, or without knowledge of the former marriage,
      they shall, after the impediment to their marriage has been removed by the death of
      the other party to the former marriage or by annulment or divorce, if they continue
      to live together as husband and wife in good faith on the part of one of them, be
      held to have been legally married from and immediately after the date of death or
      the date of the decree of annulment or divorce.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 17. Miscellaneous Provisions Relating to Marriage›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1704. Marriage between persons of the same sex
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 17. Miscellaneous Provisions Relating to Marriage › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1704. Marriage between persons of the same sex
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1704. Marriage between persons of the same sex (2023)
content:
It is hereby declared to be the strong and longstanding public policy of this Commonwealth
   that marriage shall be between one man and one woman.  A marriage between persons of the same sex which was entered into in another state
   or foreign jurisdiction, even if valid where entered into, shall be void in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 19. Abolition of Actions for Alienation of Affections and Breach of Promise to Marry›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1904. Filing or threatening to file actions prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 19. Abolition of Actions for Alienation of Affections and Breach of Promise to Marry › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1904. Filing or threatening to file actions prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1904. Filing or threatening to file actions prohibited (2023)
content:
It is unlawful for a person, either as litigant or attorney, to file, cause to be
   filed, threaten to file or threaten to cause to be filed in a court in this Commonwealth
   any pleading or paper setting forth or seeking to recover upon any cause of action
   abolished or barred by this chapter whether the cause of action arose within or without
   this Commonwealth.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Short title of part (2023)
content: This part shall be known and may be cited as the “Adoption Act.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 19. Abolition of Actions for Alienation of Affections and Breach of Promise to Marry›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1903. Purpose of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 19. Abolition of Actions for Alienation of Affections and Breach of Promise to Marry › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1903. Purpose of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1903. Purpose of chapter (2023)
content:

      Commonwealth, to a cause of action abolished by this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part II. Marriage›Chapter 19. Abolition of Actions for Alienation of Affections and Breach of Promise to Marry›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1905. Instruments executed in satisfaction of abolished claims prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part II. Marriage › Chapter 19. Abolition of Actions for Alienation of Affections and Breach of Promise to Marry › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1905. Instruments executed in satisfaction of abolished claims prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 1905. Instruments executed in satisfaction of abolished claims prohibited (2023)
content:
(a) Contracts and instruments void.--All contracts and instruments of every kind executed within this Commonwealth in payment,
      satisfaction, settlement or compromise of any claim or cause of action abolished or
      barred by this chapter, whether the claim or cause of action arose within or without
      this Commonwealth, are contrary to the public policy of this Commonwealth and void.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 23. Jurisdiction and Parties›Subchapter A. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2301. Court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 23. Jurisdiction and Parties › Subchapter A. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2301. Court

   original jurisdiction over voluntary relinquishment, involuntary termination and adoption
   proceedings.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 23. Jurisdiction and Parties › Subchapter B. Parties › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2311. Who may be adopted

content: Any individual may be adopted, regardless of his age or residence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 23. Jurisdiction and Parties›Subchapter B. Parties›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2312. Who may adopt
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 23. Jurisdiction and Parties › Subchapter B. Parties › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2312. Who may adopt
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2312. Who may adopt (2023)
content: Any individual may become an adopting parent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 23. Jurisdiction and Parties›Subchapter B. Parties›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2313. Representation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 23. Jurisdiction and Parties › Subchapter B. Parties › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2313. Representation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2313. Representation (2023)
content:
(a) Child.--The court shall appoint counsel to represent the child in an involuntary termination
      proceeding when the proceeding is being contested by one or both of the parents.  The court may appoint counsel or a guardian ad litem to represent any child who
      has not reached the age of 18 years and is subject to any other proceeding under this
      part whenever it is in the best interests of the child.  No attorney or law firm shall represent both the child and the adopting parent or
      parents.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Relinquishment to adult intending to adopt child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Relinquishment to adult intending to adopt child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Relinquishment to adult intending to adopt child (2023)
content:
(a) Petition.--When any child under the age of 18 years has been for a minimum period of three days
      in the exclusive care of an adult or adults who have filed a report of intention to
      adopt required by section 2531 (relating to report of intention to adopt), the parent
      or parents of the child may petition the court for permission to relinquish forever
      all parental rights to their child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Subchapter B. Parties›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2311. Who may be adopted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Subchapter B. Parties › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2311. Who may be adopted
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2311. Who may be adopted (2023)
content: Any individual may be adopted, regardless of his age or residence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504.1. Confidentiality
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504.1. Confidentiality
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504.1. Confidentiality (2023)
content:
The court shall take such steps as are reasonably necessary to assure that the identity
   of the adoptive parent or parents is not disclosed without their consent in any proceeding
   under this subchapter or Subchapter B (relating to involuntary termination). The Supreme Court may prescribe uniform rules under this section relating to such
   confidentiality.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504. Alternative procedure for relinquishment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504. Alternative procedure for relinquishment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504. Alternative procedure for relinquishment (2023)
content:
(a) Petition to confirm consent to adoption.--If the parent or parents of the child have executed consents to an adoption, upon
      petition by the intermediary or, where there is no intermediary, by the adoptive parent,
      the court shall hold a hearing for the purpose of confirming a consent to an adoption
      upon expiration of the time periods under section 2711 (relating to consents necessary
      to adoption).  The original consent or consents to the adoption shall be attached to the petition.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Subchapter B. Parties›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2312. Who may adopt
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Subchapter B. Parties › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2312. Who may adopt
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2312. Who may adopt (2023)
content: Any individual may become an adopting parent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2503. Hearing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2503. Hearing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2503. Hearing (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Upon presentation of a petition prepared pursuant to section 2501 (relating to relinquishment
      to agency) or section 2502 (relating to relinquishment to adult intending to adopt
      child), the court shall fix a time for hearing which shall not be less than ten days
      after filing of the petition.  The petitioner must appear at the hearing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Relinquishment to agency
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Relinquishment to agency
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Relinquishment to agency (2023)
content:
(a) Petition.--When any child under the age of 18 years has been in the care of an agency for a
      minimum period of three days or, whether or not the agency has the physical care of
      the child, the agency has received a written notice of the present intent to transfer
      to it custody of the child, executed by the parent, the parent or parents of the child
      may petition the court for permission to relinquish forever all parental rights and
      duties with respect to their child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Subchapter B. Parties›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2313. Representation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Subchapter B. Parties › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2313. Representation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2313. Representation (2023)
content:
(a) Child.--The court shall appoint counsel to represent the child in an involuntary termination
      proceeding when the proceeding is being contested by one or both of the parents.  The court may appoint counsel or a guardian ad litem to represent any child who
      has not reached the age of 18 years and is subject to any other proceeding under this
      part whenever it is in the best interests of the child.  No attorney or law firm shall represent both the child and the adopting parent or
      parents.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Counseling
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter A. Voluntary Relinquishment › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Counseling
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Counseling (2023)
content:
(a) List of counselors.--Any hospital or other facility providing maternity care shall provide a list of available
      counselors and counseling services compiled pursuant to subsection (b) to its maternity
      patients who are known to be considering relinquishment or termination of parental
      rights pursuant to this part.  The patient shall sign an acknowledgment of receipt of such list prior to discharge,
      a copy of which receipt shall be provided to the patient.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter B. Involuntary Termination›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2511. Grounds for involuntary termination

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2511. Grounds for involuntary termination (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The rights of a parent in regard to a child may be terminated after a petition filed
      on any of the following grounds:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter B. Involuntary Termination›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2513. Hearing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter B. Involuntary Termination › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2513. Hearing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2513. Hearing (2023)
content:
(a) Time.--The court shall fix a time for hearing on a petition filed under section 2512 (relating
      to petition for involuntary termination) which shall be not less than ten days after
      filing of the petition.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter B. Involuntary Termination›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2512. Petition for involuntary termination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter B. Involuntary Termination › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2512. Petition for involuntary termination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2512. Petition for involuntary termination (2023)
content:
(a) Who may file.--A petition to terminate parental rights with respect to a child under the age of 18
      years may be filed by any of the following:

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2534. Exhibits (2023)
content: The report of the intermediary shall have attached to it the following exhibits:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter C. Decree of Termination›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2521. Effect of decree of termination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter C. Decree of Termination › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2521. Effect of decree of termination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2521. Effect of decree of termination (2023)
content:
(a) Adoption proceeding rights extinguished.--A decree terminating all rights of a parent or a decree terminating all rights and
      duties of a parent entered by a court of competent jurisdiction shall extinguish the
      power or the right of the parent to object to or receive notice of adoption proceedings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter D. Reports and Investigation›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2535. Investigation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter D. Reports and Investigation › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2535. Investigation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2535. Investigation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--When a report required by section 2531 (relating to report of intention to adopt)
      has been filed, the court shall cause an investigation to be made and a report filed
      by a local public child care agency, a voluntary child care agency with its consent
      or an appropriate person designated by the court.  In lieu of the investigation, the court may accept an investigation made by the
      agency which placed the child and the report of investigation in such cases may be
      incorporated into the report of the intermediary required by section 2533 (relating
      to report of intermediary).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter B. Involuntary Termination›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. Special provisions when child conceived as a result of rape or incest

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. Special provisions when child conceived as a result of rape or incest (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other provision of law to the contrary, when a petition has been
   filed by a parent seeking to involuntarily terminate parental rights of the other
   parent under section 2511(a)(7) (relating to grounds for involuntary termination),
   the following apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter D. Reports and Investigation›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2530. Home study and preplacement report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter D. Reports and Investigation › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2530. Home study and preplacement report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2530. Home study and preplacement report (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No intermediary shall place a child in the physical care or custody of a prospective
      adoptive parent or parents unless a home study containing a favorable recommendation
      for placement of a child with the prospective parent or parents has been completed
      within three years prior thereto and which has been supplemented within one year prior
      thereto.  The home study shall be conducted by a local public child-care agency, an adoption
      agency or a licensed social worker designated by the court to perform such study.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2553. Registration of children
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2553. Registration of children
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2553. Registration of children (2023)
content:
(a) Mandatory registration.--PACE shall register and be responsible for the review and referral of children for
      whom parental rights have been terminated for 90 days and for whom no report of intention
      to adopt has been filed in the court of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2556. Related activities of agencies unaffected
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2556. Related activities of agencies unaffected
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2556. Related activities of agencies unaffected (2023)
content:
This subchapter shall not be construed to limit or delay actions by agencies or institutions
   to arrange for adoptions or other related matters on their own initiative and shall
   not alter or restrict the duties, authority and confidentiality of the agencies and
   institutions in those matters.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter D. Reports and Investigation›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2533. Report of intermediary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter D. Reports and Investigation › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2533. Report of intermediary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2533. Report of intermediary (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Within six months after filing the report of intention to adopt, the intermediary
      who or which arranged the adoption placement of any child under the age of 18 years
      shall make a written report under oath to the court in which the petition for adoption
      will be filed and shall thereupon forthwith notify in writing the adopting parent
      or parents of the fact that the report has been filed and the date thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2554. Responsibilities of PACE

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2554. Responsibilities of PACE (2023)
content: PACE shall be responsible for the following:

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2555. Responsibilities of public and private agencies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2555. Responsibilities of public and private agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2555. Responsibilities of public and private agencies (2023)
content:
All public and licensed private child service agencies shall register all children
   with PACE for whom parental rights have been terminated for 90 days and for whom no
   report of intention to adopt has been filed in the court of common pleas.  A public or licensed private agency may register other children as set forth in
   section 2553(b) (relating to registration of children).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2558. Retroactive application of subchapter

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2558. Retroactive application of subchapter (2023)
content: This subchapter shall apply retroactively to all children for whom:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2552. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2552. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2552. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange (2023)
content:
There shall be a Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange in the Office of Children,
   Youth and Families of the Department of Public Welfare.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2557. Regulations and staff
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter E. Pennsylvania Adoption Cooperative Exchange › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2557. Regulations and staff
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2557. Regulations and staff (2023)
content:
The department shall promulgate necessary regulations and shall hire the staff which
   is necessary to implement this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter D. Reports and Investigation›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2531. Report of intention to adopt
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter D. Reports and Investigation › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2531. Report of intention to adopt
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2531. Report of intention to adopt (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Every person now having or hereafter receiving or retaining custody or physical
      care of any child for the purpose or with the intention of adopting a child under
      the age of 18 years shall report to the court in which the petition for adoption will
      be filed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part III. Adoption›Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt›Subchapter D. Reports and Investigation›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2532. Filing of report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part III. Adoption › Chapter 25. Proceedings Prior to Petition to Adopt › Subchapter D. Reports and Investigation › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2532. Filing of report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 2532. Filing of report (2023)
content:
The report required by section 2531 (relating to report of intention to adopt) shall
   be filed within 30 days after the date of receipt of the custody or physical care
   of the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 31. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3102. Legislative findings and intent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 31. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3102. Legislative findings and intent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3102. Legislative findings and intent (2023)
content:
(a) Policy.--The family is the basic unit in society and the protection and preservation of the
      family is of paramount public concern.  Therefore, it is the policy of the Commonwealth to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 31. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3104. Bases of jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 31. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3104. Bases of jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3104. Bases of jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) Jurisdiction.--The courts shall have original jurisdiction in cases of divorce and for the annulment
      of void or voidable marriages and shall determine, in conjunction with any decree
      granting a divorce or annulment, the following matters, if raised in the pleadings,
      and issue appropriate decrees or orders with reference thereto, and may retain continuing
      jurisdiction thereof:

content:
The following words and phrases when used in this part shall have the meanings given
   to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 31. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3101. Short title of part
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 31. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3101. Short title of part
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3101. Short title of part (2023)
content: This part shall be known and may be cited as the Divorce Code.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 31. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3105. Effect of agreement between parties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 31. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3105. Effect of agreement between parties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3105. Effect of agreement between parties (2023)
content:
(a) Enforcement.--A party to an agreement regarding matters within the jurisdiction of the court under
      this part, whether or not the agreement has been merged or incorporated into the decree,
      may utilize a remedy or sanction set forth in this part to enforce the agreement to
      the same extent as though the agreement had been an order of the court except as provided
      to the contrary in the agreement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3307. Defenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3307. Defenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3307. Defenses (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Existing common-law defenses are retained as to the grounds enumerated in section
      3301(a) and (b) (relating to grounds for divorce). The defenses of condonation, connivance, collusion, recrimination and provocation
      are abolished as to the grounds enumerated in section 3301(c) and (d).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3304. Grounds for annulment of void marriages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3304. Grounds for annulment of void marriages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3304. Grounds for annulment of void marriages (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Where there has been no confirmation by cohabitation following the removal of an impediment,
      the supposed or alleged marriage of a person shall be deemed void in the following
      cases:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3302. Counseling
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3302. Counseling
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3302. Counseling (2023)
content:
(a) Indignities.--Whenever indignities under section 3301(a)(6) (relating to grounds for divorce) is
      the ground for divorce, the court shall require up to a maximum of three counseling
      sessions where either of the parties requests it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter B. Procedure›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3321. Hearing by master
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter B. Procedure › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3321. Hearing by master
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3321. Hearing by master (2023)
content:
The court may appoint a master to hear testimony on all or some issues, except issues
   of custody and paternity, and return the record and a transcript of the testimony
   together with a report and recommendation as prescribed by general rules, or a judge
   of the court in chambers may appoint a master to hold a nonrecord hearing and to make
   recommendations and return the same to the court, in which case either party may demand
   a hearing de novo before the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3308. Action where defendant suffering from mental disorder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3308. Action where defendant suffering from mental disorder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3308. Action where defendant suffering from mental disorder (2023)
content:
If a spouse is insane or suffering from serious mental disorder, an action may be
   commenced under this part against that spouse upon any ground for divorce or annulment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3301. Grounds for divorce
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3301. Grounds for divorce
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3301. Grounds for divorce (2023)
content:
(a) Fault.--The court may grant a divorce to the innocent and injured spouse whenever it is judged
      that the other spouse has:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3309. General appearance and collusion
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3309. General appearance and collusion
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3309. General appearance and collusion (2023)
content:
The entry of a general appearance by, or in behalf of, a defendant does not constitute
   collusion.  Collusion shall be found to exist only where the parties conspired to fabricate
   grounds for divorce or annulment, agreed to and did commit perjury or perpetrated
   fraud on the court.  Negotiation and discussion of terms of property settlement and other matters arising
   by reason of contemplated divorce or annulment do not constitute collusion.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3305. Grounds for annulment of voidable marriages

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3305. Grounds for annulment of voidable marriages (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The marriage of a person shall be deemed voidable and subject to annulment in the
      following cases:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3303. Annulment of void and voidable marriages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3303. Annulment of void and voidable marriages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3303. Annulment of void and voidable marriages (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In all cases where a supposed or alleged marriage has been contracted which is void
      or voidable under this title or under applicable law, either party to the supposed
      or alleged marriage may bring an action in annulment to have it declared void in accordance
      with the procedures provided by this part and prescribed by general rules.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3306. Proceedings to determine marital status
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3306. Proceedings to determine marital status
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3306. Proceedings to determine marital status (2023)
content:
When the validity of a marriage is denied or doubted, either or both of the parties
   to the marriage may bring an action for a declaratory judgment seeking a declaration
   of the validity or invalidity of the marriage and, upon proof of the validity or invalidity
   of the marriage, the marriage shall be declared valid or invalid by decree of the
   court and, unless reversed upon appeal, the declaration shall be conclusive upon all
   persons concerned.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter B. Procedure›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3322. Jury trial
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter B. Procedure › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3322. Jury trial
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3322. Jury trial (2023)
content:
(a) Application for jury trial.--After service of the complaint in divorce or annulment on the defendant in the manner
      prescribed by general rules or entry of a general appearance for the defendant, if
      either of the parties desires any matter of fact that is affirmed by one and denied
      by the other to be tried by a jury, that party may take a rule upon the opposite party,
      to be allowed by a judge of the court, to show cause why the issues of fact set forth
      in the rule should not be tried by a jury, which rule shall be served upon the opposite
      party or counsel for the opposite party.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter C. Attacks Upon Decrees›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3331. Limitations on attacks upon decrees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter C. Attacks Upon Decrees › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3331. Limitations on attacks upon decrees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3331. Limitations on attacks upon decrees (2023)
content:
The validity of a decree of divorce or annulment issued by a court shall not be questioned,
   except by appeal, in any court or place in this Commonwealth after the death of either
   party to the proceeding.  If it is shown that a party who subsequently attempts to question the validity of
   the decree had full knowledge of the facts and circumstances later complained of at
   the time of issuance of the decree or failed to take any action despite this knowledge
   within two years after the date of the decree, the party shall be barred from questioning
   the decree, and it shall be valid in all courts and places within this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter C. Attacks Upon Decrees›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3333. Res judicata and estoppel
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter C. Attacks Upon Decrees › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3333. Res judicata and estoppel
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3333. Res judicata and estoppel (2023)
content:
The validity of a divorce or annulment decree granted by a court having jurisdiction
   over the subject matter may not be questioned by a party who was subject to the personal
   jurisdiction of the court except by direct appeal provided or prescribed by law.  A party who sought and obtained a decree, financed or agreed to its procurement,
   or accepted a property settlement, alimony pendente lite or alimony pursuant to the
   terms of the decree, or who remarries after the decree, or is guilty of laches, is
   barred from making a collateral attack upon the validity of the decree unless, by
   clear and convincing evidence, it is established that fraud by the other party prevented
   the making of a timely appeal from the divorce or annulment decree.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status›Subchapter C. Attacks Upon Decrees›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3332. Opening or vacating decrees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Chapter 33. Dissolution of Marital Status › Subchapter C. Attacks Upon Decrees › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3332. Opening or vacating decrees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3332. Opening or vacating decrees (2023)
content:
A motion to open a decree of divorce or annulment may be made only within the period
   limited by42 Pa.C.S. § 5505(relating to modification of orders) and not thereafter.  The motion may lie where it is alleged that the decree was procured by intrinsic
   fraud or that there is new evidence relating to the cause of action which will sustain
   the attack upon its validity.  A motion to vacate a decree or strike a judgment alleged to be void because of extrinsic
   fraud, lack of jurisdiction over the subject matter or a fatal defect apparent upon
   the face of the record must be made within five years after entry of the final decree.  Intrinsic fraud relates to a matter adjudicated by the judgment, including perjury
   and false testimony, whereas extrinsic fraud relates to matters collateral to the
   judgment which have the consequence of precluding a fair hearing or presentation of
   one side of the case.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3309. General appearance and collusion
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3309. General appearance and collusion
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3309. General appearance and collusion (2023)
content:
The entry of a general appearance by, or in behalf of, a defendant does not constitute
   collusion.  Collusion shall be found to exist only where the parties conspired to fabricate
   grounds for divorce or annulment, agreed to and did commit perjury or perpetrated
   fraud on the court.  Negotiation and discussion of terms of property settlement and other matters arising
   by reason of contemplated divorce or annulment do not constitute collusion.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part IV. Divorce›Subchapter B. Procedure›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3321. Hearing by master
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part IV. Divorce › Subchapter B. Procedure › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3321. Hearing by master
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 3321. Hearing by master (2023)
content:
The court may appoint a master to hear testimony on all or some issues, except issues
   of custody and paternity, and return the record and a transcript of the testimony
   together with a report and recommendation as prescribed by general rules, or a judge
   of the court in chambers may appoint a master to hold a nonrecord hearing and to make
   recommendations and return the same to the court, in which case either party may demand
   a hearing de novo before the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part V. Support, Property and Contracts›Chapter 41. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4102. Proceedings in case of debts contracted for necessaries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part V. Support, Property and Contracts › Chapter 41. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4102. Proceedings in case of debts contracted for necessaries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 4102. Proceedings in case of debts contracted for necessaries (2023)
content:
In all cases where debts are contracted for necessaries by either spouse for the support
   and maintenance of the family, it shall be lawful for the creditor in this case to
   institute suit against the husband and wife for the price of such necessaries and,
   after obtaining a judgment, have an execution against the spouse contracting the debt
   alone;  and, if no property of that spouse is found, execution may be levied upon
   and satisfied out of the separate property of the other spouse.

content:
A married person may loan the other spouse money from the separate estate of the married
   person and take in security therefor a judgment or mortgage against the property of
   the other spouse which shall be valid as otherwise provided by law.
