title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5412. Cooperation between courts; preservation of records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5412. Cooperation between courts; preservation of records (2023)
content: (a) Assistance of another state.--A court of this Commonwealth may request the appropriate court of another state to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5423. Jurisdiction to modify determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5423. Jurisdiction to modify determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5423. Jurisdiction to modify determination (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
   a court of this Commonwealth may not modify a child custody determination made by
   a court of another state unless a court of this Commonwealth has jurisdiction to make
   an initial determination under section 5421 (a)(1) or (2) (relating to initial child
   custody jurisdiction) and:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5411. Taking testimony in another state
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5411. Taking testimony in another state
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5411. Taking testimony in another state (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In addition to other procedures available to a party, a party to a child custody proceeding
      may offer testimony of witnesses who are located in another state, including testimony
      of the parties and the child, by deposition or other means allowable in this Commonwealth
      for testimony taken in another state.  The court on its own motion may order that the testimony of a person be taken in
      another state and may prescribe the manner in which and the terms upon which the testimony
      is taken.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5406. Effect of child custody determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5406. Effect of child custody determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5406. Effect of child custody determination (2023)
content:
A child custody determination made by a court of this Commonwealth that had jurisdiction
   under this chapter binds all persons who have been served in accordance with the laws
   of this Commonwealth or notified in accordance with section 5408 (relating to notice
   to persons outside Commonwealth) or who have submitted to the jurisdiction of the
   court and who have been given an opportunity to be heard.  As to those persons, the determination is conclusive as to all decided issues of
   law and fact except to the extent the determination is modified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5428. Jurisdiction declined by reason of conduct
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5428. Jurisdiction declined by reason of conduct
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5428. Jurisdiction declined by reason of conduct (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction)
      or by other laws of this Commonwealth, if a court of this Commonwealth has jurisdiction
      under this chapter because a person seeking to invoke its jurisdiction has engaged
      in unjustifiable conduct, the court shall decline to exercise its jurisdiction unless:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5429. Information to be submitted to court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5429. Information to be submitted to court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5429. Information to be submitted to court (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject to the rules set forth in Chapter 53 (relating to child custody) providing
      for the confidentiality of procedures, addresses and other identifying information
      in a child custody proceeding, each party in its first pleading or in an attached
      affidavit shall give information, if reasonably ascertainable, under oath as to the
      child's present address or whereabouts, the places where the child has lived during
      the last five years and the names and present addresses of the persons with whom the
      child has lived during that period.  The pleading or affidavit must state whether the party:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5425. Notice; opportunity to be heard; joinder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5425. Notice; opportunity to be heard; joinder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5425. Notice; opportunity to be heard; joinder (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Before a child custody determination is made under this chapter, notice and an opportunity
      to be heard in accordance with the standards of section 5408 (relating to notice to
      persons outside Commonwealth) must be given to all persons entitled to notice under
      the laws of this Commonwealth as in child custody proceedings between residents of
      this Commonwealth, any parent whose parental rights have not been previously terminated
      and any person having physical custody of the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5421. Initial child custody jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5421. Initial child custody jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5421. Initial child custody jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
      a court of this Commonwealth has jurisdiction to make an initial child custody determination
      only if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5430. Appearance of parties and child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5430. Appearance of parties and child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5430. Appearance of parties and child (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In a child custody proceeding in this Commonwealth, the court may order a party to
      the proceeding who is in this Commonwealth to appear before the court in person with
      or without the child.  The court may order any person who is in this Commonwealth and who has physical
      custody or control of the child to appear in person with the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5426. Simultaneous proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5426. Simultaneous proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5426. Simultaneous proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
      a court of this Commonwealth may not exercise its jurisdiction under this subchapter
      if, at the time of the commencement of the proceeding, a proceeding concerning the
      custody of the child has been commenced in a court of another state having jurisdiction
      substantially in conformity with this chapter unless the proceeding has been terminated
      or is stayed by the court of the other state because a court of this Commonwealth
      is a more convenient forum under section 5427 (relating to inconvenient forum).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5443. Duty to enforce
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5443. Duty to enforce
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5443. Duty to enforce (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth shall recognize and enforce a child custody determination
      of a court of another state if the latter court exercised jurisdiction in substantial
      conformity with this chapter or the determination was made under factual circumstances
      meeting the jurisdictional standards of this chapter and the determination has not
      been modified in accordance with this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5441. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5441. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5441. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this subchapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5445. Registration of child custody determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5445. Registration of child custody determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5445. Registration of child custody determination (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A child custody determination issued by a court of another state may be registered
      in this Commonwealth, with or without a simultaneous request for enforcement, by sending
      to the appropriate court in this Commonwealth:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5444. Temporary visitation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5444. Temporary visitation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5444. Temporary visitation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth which does not have jurisdiction to modify a child custody
      determination may issue a temporary order enforcing:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5442. Enforcement under Hague Convention
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5442. Enforcement under Hague Convention
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5442. Enforcement under Hague Convention (2023)
content:
Under this subchapter a court of this Commonwealth may enforce an order for the return
   of the child made under the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International
   Child Abduction as if it were a child custody determination.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5446. Enforcement of registered determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5446. Enforcement of registered determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5446. Enforcement of registered determination (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth may grant any relief normally available under the laws
      of this Commonwealth to enforce a registered child custody determination made by a
      court of another state.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5427. Inconvenient forum
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5427. Inconvenient forum
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5427. Inconvenient forum (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth which has jurisdiction under this chapter to make a child
      custody determination may decline to exercise its jurisdiction at any time if it determines
      that it is an inconvenient forum under the circumstances and that a court of another
      state is a more appropriate forum.  The issue of inconvenient forum may be raised upon motion of a party, the court's
      own motion or request of another court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5449. Service of petition and order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5449. Service of petition and order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5449. Service of petition and order (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided in section 5451 (relating to warrant to take physical
   custody of child), the petition and order must be served by any method authorized
   by the laws of this Commonwealth upon respondent and any person who has physical custody
   of the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5447. Simultaneous proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5447. Simultaneous proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5447. Simultaneous proceedings (2023)
content:
If a proceeding for enforcement under this subchapter is commenced in a court of this
   Commonwealth and the court determines that a proceeding to modify the determination
   is pending in a court of another state having jurisdiction to modify the determination
   under Subchapter B (relating to jurisdiction), the enforcing court shall immediately
   communicate with the modifying court.  The proceeding for enforcement continues unless the enforcing court, after consultation
   with the modifying court, stays or dismisses the proceeding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5451. Warrant to take physical custody of child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5451. Warrant to take physical custody of child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5451. Warrant to take physical custody of child (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Upon the filing of a petition seeking enforcement of a child custody determination,
      the petitioner may file a verified application for the issuance of a warrant to take
      physical custody of the child if the child is immediately likely to suffer serious
      physical harm or be removed from this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5448. Expedited enforcement of child custody determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5448. Expedited enforcement of child custody determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5448. Expedited enforcement of child custody determination (2023)
content:
(a) Verification.--A petition under this subchapter must be verified.  Certified copies of all orders sought to be enforced and of any order confirming
      registration must be attached to the petition.  A copy of a certified copy of an order may be attached instead of the original.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5450. Hearing and order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5450. Hearing and order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5450. Hearing and order (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Unless the court issues a temporary emergency order pursuant to section 5424 (relating
      to temporary emergency jurisdiction), upon a finding that a petitioner is entitled
      to immediate physical custody of the child, the court shall order that the petitioner
      may take immediate physical custody of the child unless the respondent establishes
      that:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5453. Recognition and enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5453. Recognition and enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5453. Recognition and enforcement (2023)
content:
A court of this Commonwealth shall accord full faith and credit to an order issued
   by another state and consistent with this chapter which enforces a child custody determination
   by a court of another state unless the order has been vacated, stayed or modified
   by a court having jurisdiction to do so under Subchapter B (relating to jurisdiction).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5454. Appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5454. Appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5454. Appeals (2023)
content:
An appeal may be taken from a final order in a proceeding under this subchapter in
   accordance with expedited appellate procedures in other civil cases.  Unless the court enters a temporary emergency order under section 5424 (relating
   to temporary emergency jurisdiction), the enforcing court may not stay an order enforcing
   a child custody determination pending appeal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5452. Costs, fees and expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5452. Costs, fees and expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5452. Costs, fees and expenses (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The court shall award the prevailing party, including a state, necessary and reasonable
      expenses incurred by or on behalf of the party, including costs, communication expenses,
      attorney fees, investigative fees, expenses for witnesses, travel expenses and child
      care during the course of the proceedings, unless the party from whom fees or expenses
      are sought establishes that the award would be clearly inappropriate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5404. Application to Native American tribes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5404. Application to Native American tribes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5404. Application to Native American tribes (2023)
content:
(a) Primacy of Indian Child Welfare Act.--A child custody proceeding that pertains to a Native American child as defined in
      the Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978 (Public Law 95-608,25 U.S.C. § 1901 et seq.) is not subject to this chapter to the extent that it is governed by the Indian Child
      Welfare Act of 1978.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter D. Intrastate Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5471. Intrastate application
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter D. Intrastate Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5471. Intrastate application
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5471. Intrastate application (2023)
content:
The provisions of this chapter allocating jurisdiction and functions between and among
   courts of different states shall also allocate jurisdiction and functions between
   and among the courts of common pleas of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5403. Proceedings governed by other law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5403. Proceedings governed by other law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5403. Proceedings governed by other law (2023)
content:
This chapter does not govern an adoption proceeding or a proceeding pertaining to
   the authorization of emergency medical care for a child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5456. Role of law enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5456. Role of law enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5456. Role of law enforcement (2023)
content:
At the request of a prosecutor or other appropriate public official acting under section
   5455 (relating to role of prosecutor or public official), a law enforcement officer
   may take any lawful action reasonably necessary to locate a child or a party and assist
   a prosecutor or appropriate public official with responsibilities under section 5455.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5455. Role of prosecutor or public official
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5455. Role of prosecutor or public official
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5455. Role of prosecutor or public official (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In a case arising under this chapter or involving the Hague Convention on the Civil
      Aspects of International Child Abduction, the prosecutor or other appropriate public
      official may take any lawful action, including resort to a proceeding under this subchapter
      or any other available civil proceeding to locate a child, obtain the return of a
      child or enforce a child custody determination if there is:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5481. Application and construction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5481. Application and construction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5481. Application and construction (2023)
content:
In applying and construing this chapter, consideration must be given to the need to
   promote uniformity of the law with respect to its subject matter among states that
   enact it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5407. Priority
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5407. Priority
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5407. Priority (2023)
content:
If a question of existence or exercise of jurisdiction under this chapter is raised
   in a child custody proceeding, the question, upon request of a party, must be given
   priority on the calendar and handled expeditiously.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5482. Severability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5482. Severability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5482. Severability (2023)
content:
If any provision of this chapter or its application to any person or circumstance
   is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect other provisions or applications of
   this chapter which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application,
   and to this end the provisions of this chapter are severable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5402. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5402. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5402. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5401. Short title of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5401. Short title of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5401. Short title of chapter (2023)
content:
This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction
   and Enforcement Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5406. Effect of child custody determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5406. Effect of child custody determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5406. Effect of child custody determination (2023)
content:
A child custody determination made by a court of this Commonwealth that had jurisdiction
   under this chapter binds all persons who have been served in accordance with the laws
   of this Commonwealth or notified in accordance with section 5408 (relating to notice
   to persons outside Commonwealth) or who have submitted to the jurisdiction of the
   court and who have been given an opportunity to be heard.  As to those persons, the determination is conclusive as to all decided issues of
   law and fact except to the extent the determination is modified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5457. Costs and expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Chapter 54. Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5457. Costs and expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5457. Costs and expenses (2023)
content:
If the respondent is not the prevailing party, the court may assess against the respondent
   all direct expenses and costs incurred by the prosecutor or other appropriate public
   official and law enforcement officers under section 5455 (relating to role of prosecutor
   or public official) or 5456 (relating to role of law enforcement).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5409. Appearance and limited immunity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5409. Appearance and limited immunity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5409. Appearance and limited immunity (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A party to a child custody proceeding, including a modification proceeding or a petitioner
      or respondent in a proceeding to enforce or register a child custody determination,
      is not subject to personal jurisdiction in this Commonwealth for another proceeding
      or purpose solely by reason of having participated or of having been physically present
      for the purpose of participating in the proceeding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5405. International application of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5405. International application of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5405. International application of chapter (2023)
content:
(a) Foreign country treated as state.--A court of this Commonwealth shall treat a foreign country as if it were a state of
      the United States for the purpose of applying Subchapter B (relating to jurisdiction)
      and this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5410. Communication between courts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5410. Communication between courts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5410. Communication between courts (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth may communicate with a court in another state concerning
      a proceeding arising under this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5408. Notice to persons outside Commonwealth
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5408. Notice to persons outside Commonwealth
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5408. Notice to persons outside Commonwealth (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Notice required for the exercise of jurisdiction when a person is outside this Commonwealth
      may be given in a manner prescribed by the laws of this Commonwealth for service of
      process or by the law of the state in which the service is made.  Notice must be given in a manner reasonably calculated to give actual notice but
      may be by publication if other means are not effective.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5421. Initial child custody jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5421. Initial child custody jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5421. Initial child custody jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
      a court of this Commonwealth has jurisdiction to make an initial child custody determination
      only if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5412. Cooperation between courts; preservation of records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5412. Cooperation between courts; preservation of records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5412. Cooperation between courts; preservation of records (2023)
content: (a) Assistance of another state.--A court of this Commonwealth may request the appropriate court of another state to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5422. Exclusive, continuing jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5422. Exclusive, continuing jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5422. Exclusive, continuing jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
      a court of this Commonwealth which has made a child custody determination consistent
      with section 5421 (relating to initial child custody jurisdiction) or 5423 (relating
      to jurisdiction to modify determination) has exclusive, continuing jurisdiction over
      the determination until:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5424. Temporary emergency jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5424. Temporary emergency jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5424. Temporary emergency jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth has temporary emergency jurisdiction if the child is
      present in this Commonwealth and the child has been abandoned or it is necessary in
      an emergency to protect the child because the child or a sibling or parent of the
      child is subjected to or threatened with mistreatment or abuse.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5425. Notice; opportunity to be heard; joinder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5425. Notice; opportunity to be heard; joinder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5425. Notice; opportunity to be heard; joinder (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Before a child custody determination is made under this chapter, notice and an opportunity
      to be heard in accordance with the standards of section 5408 (relating to notice to
      persons outside Commonwealth) must be given to all persons entitled to notice under
      the laws of this Commonwealth as in child custody proceedings between residents of
      this Commonwealth, any parent whose parental rights have not been previously terminated
      and any person having physical custody of the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5411. Taking testimony in another state
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5411. Taking testimony in another state
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5411. Taking testimony in another state (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In addition to other procedures available to a party, a party to a child custody proceeding
      may offer testimony of witnesses who are located in another state, including testimony
      of the parties and the child, by deposition or other means allowable in this Commonwealth
      for testimony taken in another state.  The court on its own motion may order that the testimony of a person be taken in
      another state and may prescribe the manner in which and the terms upon which the testimony
      is taken.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5430. Appearance of parties and child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5430. Appearance of parties and child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5430. Appearance of parties and child (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In a child custody proceeding in this Commonwealth, the court may order a party to
      the proceeding who is in this Commonwealth to appear before the court in person with
      or without the child.  The court may order any person who is in this Commonwealth and who has physical
      custody or control of the child to appear in person with the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5428. Jurisdiction declined by reason of conduct
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5428. Jurisdiction declined by reason of conduct
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5428. Jurisdiction declined by reason of conduct (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction)
      or by other laws of this Commonwealth, if a court of this Commonwealth has jurisdiction
      under this chapter because a person seeking to invoke its jurisdiction has engaged
      in unjustifiable conduct, the court shall decline to exercise its jurisdiction unless:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5442. Enforcement under Hague Convention
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5442. Enforcement under Hague Convention
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5442. Enforcement under Hague Convention (2023)
content:
Under this subchapter a court of this Commonwealth may enforce an order for the return
   of the child made under the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International
   Child Abduction as if it were a child custody determination.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5423. Jurisdiction to modify determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5423. Jurisdiction to modify determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5423. Jurisdiction to modify determination (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
   a court of this Commonwealth may not modify a child custody determination made by
   a court of another state unless a court of this Commonwealth has jurisdiction to make
   an initial determination under section 5421 (a)(1) or (2) (relating to initial child
   custody jurisdiction) and:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5443. Duty to enforce
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5443. Duty to enforce
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5443. Duty to enforce (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth shall recognize and enforce a child custody determination
      of a court of another state if the latter court exercised jurisdiction in substantial
      conformity with this chapter or the determination was made under factual circumstances
      meeting the jurisdictional standards of this chapter and the determination has not
      been modified in accordance with this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5444. Temporary visitation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5444. Temporary visitation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5444. Temporary visitation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth which does not have jurisdiction to modify a child custody
      determination may issue a temporary order enforcing:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5426. Simultaneous proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5426. Simultaneous proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5426. Simultaneous proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5424 (relating to temporary emergency jurisdiction),
      a court of this Commonwealth may not exercise its jurisdiction under this subchapter
      if, at the time of the commencement of the proceeding, a proceeding concerning the
      custody of the child has been commenced in a court of another state having jurisdiction
      substantially in conformity with this chapter unless the proceeding has been terminated
      or is stayed by the court of the other state because a court of this Commonwealth
      is a more convenient forum under section 5427 (relating to inconvenient forum).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5429. Information to be submitted to court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5429. Information to be submitted to court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5429. Information to be submitted to court (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject to the rules set forth in Chapter 53 (relating to child custody) providing
      for the confidentiality of procedures, addresses and other identifying information
      in a child custody proceeding, each party in its first pleading or in an attached
      affidavit shall give information, if reasonably ascertainable, under oath as to the
      child's present address or whereabouts, the places where the child has lived during
      the last five years and the names and present addresses of the persons with whom the
      child has lived during that period.  The pleading or affidavit must state whether the party:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter B. Jurisdiction›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5427. Inconvenient forum
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter B. Jurisdiction › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5427. Inconvenient forum
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5427. Inconvenient forum (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth which has jurisdiction under this chapter to make a child
      custody determination may decline to exercise its jurisdiction at any time if it determines
      that it is an inconvenient forum under the circumstances and that a court of another
      state is a more appropriate forum.  The issue of inconvenient forum may be raised upon motion of a party, the court's
      own motion or request of another court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5446. Enforcement of registered determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5446. Enforcement of registered determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5446. Enforcement of registered determination (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court of this Commonwealth may grant any relief normally available under the laws
      of this Commonwealth to enforce a registered child custody determination made by a
      court of another state.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5445. Registration of child custody determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5445. Registration of child custody determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5445. Registration of child custody determination (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A child custody determination issued by a court of another state may be registered
      in this Commonwealth, with or without a simultaneous request for enforcement, by sending
      to the appropriate court in this Commonwealth:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5447. Simultaneous proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5447. Simultaneous proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5447. Simultaneous proceedings (2023)
content:
If a proceeding for enforcement under this subchapter is commenced in a court of this
   Commonwealth and the court determines that a proceeding to modify the determination
   is pending in a court of another state having jurisdiction to modify the determination
   under Subchapter B (relating to jurisdiction), the enforcing court shall immediately
   communicate with the modifying court.  The proceeding for enforcement continues unless the enforcing court, after consultation
   with the modifying court, stays or dismisses the proceeding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5441. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5441. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5441. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this subchapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5449. Service of petition and order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5449. Service of petition and order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5449. Service of petition and order (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided in section 5451 (relating to warrant to take physical
   custody of child), the petition and order must be served by any method authorized
   by the laws of this Commonwealth upon respondent and any person who has physical custody
   of the child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6101. Short title of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6101. Short title of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6101. Short title of chapter (2023)
content: This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the Protection From Abuse Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5454. Appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5454. Appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5454. Appeals (2023)
content:
An appeal may be taken from a final order in a proceeding under this subchapter in
   accordance with expedited appellate procedures in other civil cases.  Unless the court enters a temporary emergency order under section 5424 (relating
   to temporary emergency jurisdiction), the enforcing court may not stay an order enforcing
   a child custody determination pending appeal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5453. Recognition and enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5453. Recognition and enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5453. Recognition and enforcement (2023)
content:
A court of this Commonwealth shall accord full faith and credit to an order issued
   by another state and consistent with this chapter which enforces a child custody determination
   by a court of another state unless the order has been vacated, stayed or modified
   by a court having jurisdiction to do so under Subchapter B (relating to jurisdiction).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5450. Hearing and order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5450. Hearing and order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5450. Hearing and order (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Unless the court issues a temporary emergency order pursuant to section 5424 (relating
      to temporary emergency jurisdiction), upon a finding that a petitioner is entitled
      to immediate physical custody of the child, the court shall order that the petitioner
      may take immediate physical custody of the child unless the respondent establishes
      that:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5448. Expedited enforcement of child custody determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5448. Expedited enforcement of child custody determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5448. Expedited enforcement of child custody determination (2023)
content:
(a) Verification.--A petition under this subchapter must be verified.  Certified copies of all orders sought to be enforced and of any order confirming
      registration must be attached to the petition.  A copy of a certified copy of an order may be attached instead of the original.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5451. Warrant to take physical custody of child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5451. Warrant to take physical custody of child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5451. Warrant to take physical custody of child (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Upon the filing of a petition seeking enforcement of a child custody determination,
      the petitioner may file a verified application for the issuance of a warrant to take
      physical custody of the child if the child is immediately likely to suffer serious
      physical harm or be removed from this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5455. Role of prosecutor or public official
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5455. Role of prosecutor or public official
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5455. Role of prosecutor or public official (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In a case arising under this chapter or involving the Hague Convention on the Civil
      Aspects of International Child Abduction, the prosecutor or other appropriate public
      official may take any lawful action, including resort to a proceeding under this subchapter
      or any other available civil proceeding to locate a child, obtain the return of a
      child or enforce a child custody determination if there is:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6105. Responsibilities of law enforcement agencies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6105. Responsibilities of law enforcement agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6105. Responsibilities of law enforcement agencies (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The police department of each municipal corporation, the Pennsylvania State Police
      and the sheriff of each county shall insure that all their officers, deputies and
      employees are familiar with the provisions of this chapter.  Instruction concerning protection from abuse shall be made a part of the training
      curriculum for all trainee officers and deputies.  All law enforcement agencies within this Commonwealth shall adopt a written domestic
      violence policy.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5457. Costs and expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5457. Costs and expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5457. Costs and expenses (2023)
content:
If the respondent is not the prevailing party, the court may assess against the respondent
   all direct expenses and costs incurred by the prosecutor or other appropriate public
   official and law enforcement officers under section 5455 (relating to role of prosecutor
   or public official) or 5456 (relating to role of law enforcement).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5456. Role of law enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5456. Role of law enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5456. Role of law enforcement (2023)
content:
At the request of a prosecutor or other appropriate public official acting under section
   5455 (relating to role of prosecutor or public official), a law enforcement officer
   may take any lawful action reasonably necessary to locate a child or a party and assist
   a prosecutor or appropriate public official with responsibilities under section 5455.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6103. Jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6103. Jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6103. Jurisdiction (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--The court shall have jurisdiction over all proceedings under this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6102. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6102. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6102. Definitions (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the meanings
      given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6107. Hearings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6107. Hearings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6107. Hearings (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Within ten business days of the filing of a petition under this chapter, a hearing
      shall be held before the court, at which the plaintiff must prove the allegation of
      abuse by a preponderance of the evidence.  The court shall, at the time the defendant is given notice of the hearing, advise
      the defendant of the right to be represented by counsel, of the right to present evidence,
      of the right to compel attendance of witnesses, of the method by which witnesses may
      be compelled, of the possibility that any firearm, other weapon or ammunition owned
      and any firearm license possessed may be ordered temporarily relinquished, of the
      options for relinquishment of a firearm pursuant to this chapter, of the possibility
      that Federal or State law may prohibit the possession of firearms, including an explanation
      of18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(8)(relating to unlawful acts) and18 Pa.C.S. § 6105(relating to persons not to possess, use, manufacture, control, sell or transfer
      firearms), and that any protection order granted by a court may be considered in any
      subsequent proceedings under this title.  This notice shall be printed and delivered in a manner which easily attracts attention
      to its content and shall specify that child custody is one of the proceedings where
      prior protection orders may be considered.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6106. Commencement of proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6106. Commencement of proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6106. Commencement of proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An adult or an emancipated minor may seek relief under this chapter for that person
      or any parent, adult household member or guardian ad litem may seek relief under this
      chapter on behalf of minor children, or a guardian of the person of an adult who has
      been declared incompetent under 20 Pa.C.S. Ch. 51 Subch. B (relating to appointment of guardian) may seek relief on behalf of the incompetent
      adult, by filing a petition with the court alleging abuse by the defendant.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.1. Return of relinquished firearms, other weapons and ammunition and additional relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.1. Return of relinquished firearms, other weapons and ammunition and additional relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.1. Return of relinquished firearms, other weapons and ammunition and additional relief (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any court order requiring the relinquishment of firearms, other weapons or ammunition
      shall provide for the return of the relinquished firearms, other weapons or ammunition
      to the defendant upon expiration of the order or dismissal of a petition for a protection
      from abuse order.  The defendant may take custody of the firearms, other weapons and ammunition provided
      that the defendant is otherwise eligible to lawfully possess the relinquished items.  The defendant shall not be required to pay any fees, costs or charges associated
      with the returns, whether those fees, costs or charges are imposed by the Pennsylvania
      State Police, any local law enforcement agency or any other entity, including a licensed
      importer, licensed manufacturer or licensed dealer in order to secure return of the
      relinquished firearms, other weapons or ammunition.  The sheriff's or the appropriate law enforcement agency's office shall maintain
      a weapons return form that the defendant may fill out and return to the office once
      a temporary or final protection from abuse order has been dismissed or expires.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6104. Full faith and credit and foreign protection orders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6104. Full faith and credit and foreign protection orders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6104. Full faith and credit and foreign protection orders (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A court shall recognize and enforce a valid foreign protection order issued by a comparable
      court.  The validity of a foreign protection order shall only be determined by a court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.4. Registry or database of firearm ownership
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.4. Registry or database of firearm ownership
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.4. Registry or database of firearm ownership (2023)
content:
(a) Confidentiality.--Information retained to ensure compliance with this chapter and to document the return
      of firearms shall not be subject to access under the act of June 21, 1957 (P.L. 390,
      No. 212),1referred to as the Right-to-Know Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VI. Children and Minors›Subchapter C. Enforcement›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5452. Costs, fees and expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VI. Children and Minors › Subchapter C. Enforcement › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5452. Costs, fees and expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 5452. Costs, fees and expenses (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The court shall award the prevailing party, including a state, necessary and reasonable
      expenses incurred by or on behalf of the party, including costs, communication expenses,
      attorney fees, investigative fees, expenses for witnesses, travel expenses and child
      care during the course of the proceedings, unless the party from whom fees or expenses
      are sought establishes that the award would be clearly inappropriate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108. Relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108. Relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108. Relief (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject to subsection (a.1), the court may grant any protection order or approve any
      consent agreement to bring about a cessation of abuse of the plaintiff or minor children.  The order or agreement may include:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.2. Relinquishment for consignment sale, lawful transfer or safekeeping
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.2. Relinquishment for consignment sale, lawful transfer or safekeeping
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.2. Relinquishment for consignment sale, lawful transfer or safekeeping (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a defendant who is the subject of a final
      protection from abuse order, which order provides for the relinquishment of firearms,
      other weapons or ammunition during the period of time the order is in effect, may,
      within the time frame specified in the order and in lieu of relinquishment to the
      sheriff or the appropriate law enforcement agency, relinquish to a dealer licensed
      pursuant to18 Pa.C.S. § 6113(relating to licensing of dealers) any firearms, other weapons or ammunition for
      consignment sale, lawful transfer or safekeeping.  The dealer may charge the defendant a reasonable fee for accepting relinquishment
      and for storage of any firearms, other weapons or ammunition.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6109. Service of orders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6109. Service of orders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6109. Service of orders (2023)
content:
(a) Issuance.--A copy of an order under this chapter shall be issued to the plaintiff, the defendant
      and the police department with appropriate jurisdiction to enforce the order or agreement
      in accordance with the provisions of this chapter or as ordered by the court or hearing
      officer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6111. Domestic violence counselor/advocate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6111. Domestic violence counselor/advocate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6111. Domestic violence counselor/advocate (2023)
content:
A domestic violence counselor/advocate may accompany a party to any legal proceeding
   or hearing under this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6113. Arrest for violation of order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6113. Arrest for violation of order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6113. Arrest for violation of order (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An arrest for violation of an order issued pursuant to this chapter or a foreign protection
      order may be without warrant upon probable cause whether or not the violation is committed
      in the presence of the police officer or sheriff in circumstances where the defendant
      has violated a provision of an order consistent with section 6108(a)(1), (2), (3),
      (4), (6), (7), (9) or (9.1) (relating to relief).  The police officer or sheriff may verify the existence of a protection order by
      telephone, radio or other electronic communication with the appropriate police department,
      Pennsylvania State Police registry, protection order file or issuing authority.  A police officer or sheriff shall arrest a defendant for violating an order issued
      under this chapter by a court within the judicial district, issued by a court in another
      judicial district within this Commonwealth or a foreign protection order issued by
      a comparable court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6114.1. Civil contempt or modification for violation of an order or agreement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6114.1. Civil contempt or modification for violation of an order or agreement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6114.1. Civil contempt or modification for violation of an order or agreement (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A plaintiff may file a petition for civil contempt with the issuing court alleging
      that the defendant has violated any provision of an order or court-approved agreement
      issued under this chapter or a foreign protection order.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.7. Order to seal record from public view
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.7. Order to seal record from public view
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.7. Order to seal record from public view (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, an individual who has entered
      into a consent agreement approved by the court under section 6108(a) (relating to
      relief) may petition the court for an order to seal the record of the individual from
      public view.  The court may grant the order if the petitioner proves all of the following by clear
      and convincing evidence:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.3. Relinquishment to third party for safekeeping
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.3. Relinquishment to third party for safekeeping
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.3. Relinquishment to third party for safekeeping (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A defendant who is the subject of a protection from abuse order, which order provides
      for the relinquishment of firearms, other weapons or ammunition during the period
      of time the order is in effect, may, within the time frame specified in the order
      and in lieu of relinquishment to the sheriff, relinquish any firearms, other weapons
      or ammunition for safekeeping to a third party who meets the requirements of a third
      party under subsection (b)(3).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6115. Reporting abuse and immunity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6115. Reporting abuse and immunity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6115. Reporting abuse and immunity (2023)
content:
(a) Reporting.--A person having reasonable cause to believe that a person is being abused may report
      the information to the local police department.

content:
In addition to any other penalty provided by 18 Pa.C.S. Ch. 61 Subch. A (relating to Uniform Firearms Act), a commercial armory which violates the provisions
   of this chapter regarding safekeeping shall forfeit all Federal and State licenses
   related to firearms.
