path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6113.1. Private criminal complaints for violation of order or agreement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6113.1. Private criminal complaints for violation of order or agreement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6113.1. Private criminal complaints for violation of order or agreement (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A plaintiff may file a private criminal complaint against a defendant, alleging indirect
      criminal contempt for a noneconomic violation of any provision of an order or court-approved
      consent agreement issued under this chapter or a foreign protection order, with the
      court, the office of the district attorney or the magisterial district judge in the
      jurisdiction or county where the violation occurred, except that, in a city of the
      first class, a complaint may only be filed with the family division of the court of
      common pleas or the office of the district attorney.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6112. Disclosure of addresses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6112. Disclosure of addresses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6112. Disclosure of addresses (2023)
content:
During the course of a proceeding under this chapter, the court or hearing officer
   may consider whether the plaintiff or plaintiff's family is endangered by disclosure
   of the permanent or temporary address of the plaintiff or minor children.  Neither in the pleadings nor during proceedings or hearings under this chapter shall
   the court or hearing officer require disclosure of the address of a domestic violence
   program.  Where the court concludes that the defendant poses a threat of continued danger
   to the plaintiff and where the plaintiff requests that his or her address, telephone
   number and information about whereabouts not be disclosed, the court shall enter an
   order directing that law enforcement agencies, human service agencies and school districts
   (both in which a plaintiff's child in custody of the plaintiff is or has been enrolled)
   shall not disclose the presence of the plaintiff or the child in the jurisdiction
   or district or furnish any address, telephone number or any other demographic information
   about the plaintiff and child except by further order of the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6114. Contempt for violation of order or agreement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6114. Contempt for violation of order or agreement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6114. Contempt for violation of order or agreement (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Where the police, sheriff or the plaintiff have filed charges of indirect criminal
      contempt against a defendant for violation of a protection order issued under this
      chapter, a foreign protection order or a court-approved consent agreement, the court
      may hold the defendant in indirect criminal contempt and punish the defendant in accordance
      with law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6116. Confidentiality
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6116. Confidentiality
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6116. Confidentiality (2023)
content:
Unless a victim waives the privilege in a signed writing prior to testimony or disclosure,
   a domestic violence counselor/advocate or a coparticipant who is present during domestic
   violence counseling/advocacy shall not be competent nor permitted to testify or to
   otherwise disclose confidential communications made to or by the counselor/advocate
   by or to a victim.  The privilege shall terminate upon the death of the victim.  Neither the domestic violence counselor/advocate nor the victim shall waive the
   privilege of confidential communications by reporting facts of physical or sexual
   assault under Chapter 63 (relating to child protective services), a Federal or State
   mandatory reporting statute or a local mandatory reporting ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.5. Penalties for release of information
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.5. Penalties for release of information
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6108.5. Penalties for release of information (2023)
content:
Any person who violates section 6108(a)(7)(v) (relating to relief) by releasing information
   with the intent and purpose of committing such violation commits a misdemeanor of
   the third degree.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6117. Procedure and other remedies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6117. Procedure and other remedies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6117. Procedure and other remedies (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Unless otherwise indicated in this chapter, a proceeding under this chapter shall
      be in accordance with applicable general rules and shall be in addition to any other
      available civil or criminal remedies.  The plaintiff and the defendant may seek modification of an order issued under section
      6108 (relating to relief) at any time during the pendency of an order.  Except as otherwise indicated in this chapter, modification may be ordered after
      the filing of a petition for modification, service of the petition and a hearing on
      the petition.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6120. Inability to pay
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6120. Inability to pay
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6120. Inability to pay (2023)
content:
(a) Order for installment payments.--Upon plea and proof that a person is without the financial means to pay a fine, a
      fee, economic relief ordered under section 6108(a)(8) (relating to relief) or a cost,
      a court may order payment of money owed in installments appropriate to the circumstances
      of the person and shall fix the amounts, times and manner of payment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6121. Warrantless searches
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6121. Warrantless searches
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6121. Warrantless searches (2023)
content:
Except as provided in section 6113 (relating to arrest for violation of order), nothing
   in this chapter shall authorize a warrantless search for firearms, other weapons or
   ammunition.

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6122. Construction

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6119. Immunity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 61. Protection from Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6119. Immunity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6119. Immunity (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Law enforcement agencies and their employees, including police officers and sheriffs,
      shall, except as provided in subsection (b), be immune from civil liability for actions
      taken in good faith to carry out their duties relating to the seizure and relinquishment
      of firearms, other weapons and ammunition as provided for in this chapter, except
      for gross negligence, intentional misconduct or reckless, willful or wanton misconduct.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6304. Exclusions from child abuse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6304. Exclusions from child abuse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6304. Exclusions from child abuse (2023)
content:
(a) Environmental factors.--No child shall be deemed to be physically or mentally abused based on injuries that
      result solely from environmental factors, such as inadequate housing, furnishings,
      income, clothing and medical care, that are beyond the control of the parent or person
      responsible for the child's welfare with whom the child resides.  This subsection shall not apply to any child-care service as defined in this chapter,
      excluding an adoptive parent.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter B. Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6314. Photographs, medical tests and X-rays of child subject to report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6314. Photographs, medical tests and X-rays of child subject to report (2023)
content:
A person or official required to report cases of suspected child abuse may take or
   cause to be taken photographs of the child who is subject to a report and, if clinically
   indicated, cause to be performed a radiological examination and other medical tests
   on the child.  Medical summaries or reports of the photographs, X-rays and relevant medical tests
   taken shall be sent to the county agency at the time the written report is sent or
   within 48 hours after a report is made by electronic technologies or as soon thereafter
   as possible.  The county agency shall have access to actual photographs or duplicates and X-rays
   and may obtain them or duplicates of them upon request.  Medical summaries or reports of the photographs, X-rays and relevant medical tests
   shall be made available to law enforcement officials in the course of investigating
   cases pursuant to section 6340(a)(9) or (10) (relating to release of information in
   confidential reports).

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6312. Persons encouraged to report suspected child abuse (2023)
content:
Any person may make an oral or written report of suspected child abuse, which may
   be submitted electronically, or cause a report of suspected child abuse to be made
   to the department, county agency or law enforcement, if that person has reasonable
   cause to suspect that a child is a victim of child abuse.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter B. Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6316. Admission to private and public hospitals

Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6316. Admission to private and public hospitals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6316. Admission to private and public hospitals (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Children appearing to suffer any physical or mental condition which may constitute
      child abuse shall be admitted to, treated and maintained in facilities of private
      and public hospitals on the basis of medical need and shall not be refused or deprived
      in any way of proper medical treatment and care.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter B. Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6317. Mandatory reporting and postmortem investigation of deaths
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter B. Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6317. Mandatory reporting and postmortem investigation of deaths
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6317. Mandatory reporting and postmortem investigation of deaths (2023)
content:
A person or official required to report cases of suspected child abuse, including
   employees of a county agency, who has reasonable cause to suspect that a child died
   as a result of child abuse shall report that suspicion to the appropriate coroner
   or medical examiner.  The coroner or medical examiner shall accept the report for investigation and shall
   report his finding to the police, the district attorney, the appropriate county agency
   and, if the report is made by a hospital, the hospital.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6332. Establishment of Statewide toll-free telephone number
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6332. Establishment of Statewide toll-free telephone number
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6332. Establishment of Statewide toll-free telephone number (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The department shall establish a single Statewide toll-free telephone number that
      all persons, whether mandated by law or not, may use to report cases of suspected
      child abuse or children allegedly in need of general protective services.  A county agency or law enforcement official shall use the Statewide toll-free telephone
      number or electronic technologies for determining the existence of reports of child
      abuse or general protective services reports in the Statewide database or reports
      under investigation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6333. Continuous availability of department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6333. Continuous availability of department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6333. Continuous availability of department (2023)
content:
The department shall be capable of receiving oral reports of child abuse, reports
   of children in need of general protective services, reports made by electronic technologies
   pursuant to this chapter and report summaries from county agencies.  The department shall be capable of immediately identifying prior reports in the
   Statewide database and reports under investigation with a pending status and of monitoring
   the provision of child protective services 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6339. Confidentiality of reports (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided in this subchapter or by the Pennsylvania Rules of Juvenile
   Court Procedure, reports made pursuant to this chapter, including, but not limited
   to, report summaries of child abuse and reports made pursuant to section 6313 (relating
   to reporting procedure) as well as any other information obtained, reports written
   or photographs or X-rays taken concerning alleged instances of child abuse in the
   possession of the department or a county agency shall be confidential.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6337. Disposition and expunction of unfounded reports and general protective services reports
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6337. Disposition and expunction of unfounded reports and general protective services reports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6337. Disposition and expunction of unfounded reports and general protective services reports (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--When a report of suspected child abuse is determined by the appropriate county agency
      to be an unfounded report, the information concerning that report of suspected child
      abuse shall be maintained for a period of one year.  Following the expiration of one year after the date the report was received by the
      department, the report shall be expunged from the Statewide database, as soon as possible,
      but no later than 120 days after the one-year period following the date the report
      was received by the department, and no information other than that authorized by subsection
      (b), which shall not include any identifying information on any subject of the report,
      shall be retained by the department.  The expunction shall be mandated and guaranteed by the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6335. Access to information in Statewide database
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6335. Access to information in Statewide database
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6335. Access to information in Statewide database (2023)
content:
(a) Request for information.--A county agency or law enforcement official shall use the Statewide toll-free telephone
      number, or any manner prescribed by the department, to determine the existence of
      any prior reports involving a subject of the report.  If the Statewide database contains information related to a report or a pending
      investigation or assessment concerning a subject of the report, the department shall
      immediately convey this information to the county agency or law enforcement official.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6334. Disposition of complaints received
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6334. Disposition of complaints received
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6334. Disposition of complaints received (2023)
content:
(a) Receipt of reports by county agencies and law enforcement.--After ensuring the immediate safety of the child and any other child in the child's
      home, a county agency or law enforcement official that receives a report of suspected
      child abuse shall immediately notify the department of the report.  If the report is an oral report by telephone, the county agency or law enforcement
      official shall attempt to collect as much of the information listed in section 6313(c)
      (relating to reporting procedure) as possible and shall submit the information to
      the department within 48 hours through a report in writing or by electronic technologies.

content:
(a) General rule.--When a report of suspected child abuse is determined by the appropriate county agency
      to be a founded report or an indicated report, the status of the report shall be changed
      from pending to founded or indicated in the Statewide database.  Notice of the determination that a report is a founded, indicated or unfounded report
      shall be made as provided in section 6368(f) (relating to investigation of reports).

      or when five years have elapsed since the perpetrator's name was added to the database,
      whichever is later, if the individual meets all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6343. Investigating performance of county agency
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6343. Investigating performance of county agency
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6343. Investigating performance of county agency (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If, within 30 days from the date of an initial report of suspected child abuse, the
      appropriate county agency has not investigated the report and informed the department
      that the report is an indicated report or an unfounded report or unless within that
      same 30-day period the report is determined to be a founded report, the department
      shall have the authority to begin an inquiry into the performance of the county agency
      which inquiry may include a performance audit of the county agency as provided in
      subsection (b).  On the basis of that inquiry, the department shall take appropriate action to require
      that the provisions of this chapter be strictly followed, which action may include,
      without limitation, the institution of appropriate legal action and the withholding
      of reimbursement for all or part of the activities of the county agency.  The department shall determine in its review whether the county agency has sufficiently
      documented reasons why the investigation has not been completed in the 30-day period.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6343.1. Citizen review panels

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6343.1. Citizen review panels (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--The department shall establish a minimum of three citizen review panels.  The department may designate a child fatality or near fatality review team under
      section 6365(d) (relating to services for prevention, investigation and treatment
      of child abuse) as a citizen review panel as long as the team has the capacity to
      perform as a citizen review panel.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6344.1. Information relating to certified or licensed child-care home residents (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In addition to the requirements of section 6344 (relating to employees having contact
      with children;  adoptive and foster parents), an individual who applies to the department
      for a certificate of compliance or a license to provide child day care in a residence
      shall include criminal history record and child abuse record information required
      under section 6344(b) for every individual 18 years of age or older who resides in
      the home for at least 30 days in a calendar year.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6342. Studies of data in records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6342. Studies of data in records (2023)
content:
(a) Studies.--The department may conduct or authorize the conducting of studies of the data contained
      in the Statewide database and by county agencies and distribute the results of the
      studies.  No study may contain the name or other information by which a subject of a report
      could be identified.  The department may allow Federal auditors access to nonidentifiable duplicates of
      reports in the Statewide database if required for Federal financial participation
      in funding of agencies.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6347. Reports to Governor and General Assembly
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6347. Reports to Governor and General Assembly
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6347. Reports to Governor and General Assembly (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No later than May 1 of every year, the secretary shall prepare and transmit to the
      Governor and the General Assembly a report on the operations of the Statewide database
      and protective services provided by county agencies.  The report shall include a full statistical analysis of the reports of suspected
      child abuse made to the department and the reports of general protective services
      made to the department or county agencies, together with a report on the implementation
      of this chapter and its total cost to the Commonwealth, the evaluation of the secretary
      of services offered under this chapter and recommendations for repeal or for additional
      legislation to fulfill the purposes of this chapter.  All such recommendations should contain an estimate of increased or decreased costs
      resulting therefrom.  The report shall also include an explanation of services provided to children who
      were the subjects of founded or indicated reports while receiving child-care services.  The department shall also describe its actions in respect to the perpetrators of
      the abuse.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6345. Audits by Attorney General
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6345. Audits by Attorney General
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6345. Audits by Attorney General (2023)
content:
The Attorney General shall conduct a mandated audit done randomly but at least once
   during each year on an unannounced basis to ensure that the expunction requirements
   of this chapter are being fully and properly conducted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6344.2. Volunteers having contact with children
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6344.2. Volunteers having contact with children
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6344.2. Volunteers having contact with children (2023)
content:
(a) Applicability.--This section applies to an adult applying for or holding an unpaid position as a volunteer
      with a child-care service, a school or a program, activity or service, as a person
      responsible for the child's welfare or having direct volunteer contact with children
      and an individual identified under section 6344(a)(5)(ii) (relating to employees having
      contact with children;  adoptive and foster parents).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6346. Cooperation of other agencies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter C. Powers and Duties of Department › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6346. Cooperation of other agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6346. Cooperation of other agencies (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The secretary may request and shall receive from Commonwealth agencies, political
      subdivisions, an authorized agency or any other agency providing services under the
      local protective services plan any assistance and data that will enable the department
      and the county agency to fulfill their responsibilities properly, including law enforcement
      officials when assistance is needed in conducting an investigation or an assessment
      of safety or risk to the child.  School districts shall cooperate with the department and the agency by providing
      them upon request with the information as is consistent with law.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6364. Purchasing services of other agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6364. Purchasing services of other agencies (2023)
content:
Any other provision of law notwithstanding but consistent with sections 6361 (relating
   to organization for child protective services) and 6362 (relating to responsibilities
   of county agency for child protective services), the county agency, based upon the
   plan of services as provided in section 6363 (relating to county plan for protective
   services), may purchase and utilize the services of any appropriate public or private
   agency.

   as required by the act of June 13, 1967 (P.L. 31, No. 21), known as the Public Welfare

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6362. Responsibilities of county agency for child protective services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6362. Responsibilities of county agency for child protective services (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The county agency shall be the sole civil agency responsible for receiving and investigating
      all reports of child abuse made pursuant to this chapter, specifically including,
      but not limited to, reports of child abuse in facilities operated by the department
      and other public agencies, for the purpose of providing protective services to prevent
      further abuses to children and to provide or arrange for and monitor the provision
      of those services necessary to safeguard and ensure the well-being and development
      of the child and to preserve and stabilize family life wherever appropriate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6366. Continuous availability to receive reports

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6366. Continuous availability to receive reports (2023)
content:
Each county agency shall receive 24 hours a day, seven days a week, all reports, both
   oral and written, of suspected child abuse in accordance with this chapter, the county
   plan for the provision of child protective services and the regulations of the department.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6370. Voluntary or court-ordered services; findings of child abuse (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Based on the investigation and evaluation conducted pursuant to this chapter, the
      county agency shall provide or contract with private or public agencies for the protection
      of the child at home whenever possible and those services necessary for adequate care
      of the child when placed in protective custody.  Prior to offering these services to a family, the agency shall explain that it has
      no legal authority to compel the family to receive the services but may inform the
      family of the obligations and authority of the county agency to initiate appropriate
      court proceedings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6372. Protecting well-being of children maintained outside home
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6372. Protecting well-being of children maintained outside home
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6372. Protecting well-being of children maintained outside home (2023)
content:
The county agency shall be as equally vigilant of the status, well-being and conditions
   under which a child is living and being maintained in a facility other than that of
   a parent, custodian or guardian from which the child has been removed as the service
   is of the conditions in the dwelling of the parent, custodian or guardian.  Where the county agency finds that the placement for any temporary or permanent
   custody, care or treatment is for any reason inappropriate or harmful in any way to
   the physical or mental well-being of the child, it shall take immediate steps to remedy
   these conditions including petitioning the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6367. Reports to department and coroner
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6367. Reports to department and coroner
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6367. Reports to department and coroner (2023)
content:
(a) Reports to department.--Upon the receipt of each report of suspected child abuse made pursuant to this chapter,
      the county agency shall immediately transmit a child abuse report summary as provided
      in section 6313 (relating to reporting procedure) to the department.  Supplemental reports shall be made at regular intervals thereafter in a manner and
      form the department prescribes by regulation to the end that the department is kept
      fully informed and up-to-date concerning the status of reports of child abuse.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6371. Rehabilitative services for child and family

Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6371. Rehabilitative services for child and family
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6371. Rehabilitative services for child and family (2023)
content:
The county agency shall provide or arrange for and monitor rehabilitative services
   for children and their families on a voluntary basis or under a final or intermediate
   order of the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6368. Investigation of reports

content:
(a) Response to direct reports.--Upon receipt of a report of suspected child abuse by a perpetrator from an individual,
      the county agency shall ensure the safety of the child and any other child in the
      child's home and immediately contact the department in accordance with the provisions
      of section 6334 (relating to disposition of complaints received).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6381. Evidence in court proceedings

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6381. Evidence in court proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In addition to the rules of evidence provided under 42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 63 (relating to
      juvenile matters), the rules of evidence in this section shall govern in child abuse
      proceedings in court or in any department administrative hearing pursuant to section
      6341 (relating to amendment or expunction of information).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6365. Services for prevention, investigation and treatment of child abuse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6365. Services for prevention, investigation and treatment of child abuse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6365. Services for prevention, investigation and treatment of child abuse (2023)
content:
(a) Instruction and education.--Each county agency shall make available among its services for the prevention and
      treatment of child abuse instruction and education for parenthood and parenting skills,
      protective and preventive social counseling, outreach and counseling services to prevent
      newborn abandonment, emergency caretaker services, emergency shelter care, emergency
      medical services and the establishment of self-help groups organized for the prevention
      and treatment of child abuse, part-day services, out-of-home placement services, therapeutic
      activities for child and family directed at alleviating conditions that present a
      risk to the safety and well-being of a child and any other services required by department
      regulations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6375. County agency requirements for general protective services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6375. County agency requirements for general protective services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6375. County agency requirements for general protective services (2023)
content:
(a) Duties of county agency.--The county agency shall make available a program of general protective services within
      each agency.  The county agency shall perform those functions assigned by this chapter and others
      that would further the purposes of this chapter.  It shall have sufficient staff of sufficient qualifications to fulfill the purposes
      of this chapter and be organized in a way as to maximize the continuity of responsibility,
      care and service of individual workers toward individual children and families.  The department by regulation shall set forth staff-to-family ratios for the receipt
      and assessment of reports of children in need of protective services and for the provision
      of services to neglected children and their families.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6376. Appeals with respect to general protective services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6376. Appeals with respect to general protective services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6376. Appeals with respect to general protective services (2023)
content:
(a) Right to appeal.--A custodial parent or person who has primary responsibility for the welfare of a child
      may appeal the county agency's decision to accept the family for services.  Written notice of this right, along with an explanation of the agency's decision,
      shall be given to the family within seven days of the decision to accept for service.  The department has no authority to modify an order of a court of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6378. Purchase of services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6378. Purchase of services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6378. Purchase of services (2023)
content:
Except for the receipt and assessment of reports alleging a need for protective services,
   the county agency may purchase and utilize the services of any appropriate public
   or private agency.  The department shall promulgate regulations establishing standards and qualifications
   of persons or agencies providing services for a county agency.  The department may, by regulation, provide for the establishment of regional facilities
   or a regional coordination of licensed professional service providers to provide county
   agencies with access to licensed physicians and psychologists, as required by this
   section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter D. Organization and Responsibilities of Child Protective Service›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6374. Principles and goals of general protective services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter D. citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6374. Principles and goals of general protective services (2023)
content:
(a) Primary purpose.--The primary purpose of general protective services is to protect the rights and welfare
      of children so that they have an opportunity for healthy growth and development.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6385. Reimbursement to county agencies

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6385. Reimbursement to county agencies (2023)
content:
The department shall certify in accordance with the needs-based budgeting provisions
   of Article VII of the act of June 13, 1967 (P.L. 31, No. 21), known as the Public
   Welfare Code,1a level of funds sufficient to meet the cost of services required by the provisions
   of this chapter which are reasonable and allowable as defined in Article VII.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Chapter 63. Child Protective Services›Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6383. Education and training
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Chapter 63. Child Protective Services › Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6383. Education and training
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6383. Education and training (2023)
content:
(a) Duties of department and county agencies.--The department and each county agency, both jointly and individually, shall conduct
      a continuing publicity and education program for the citizens of this Commonwealth
      aimed at the prevention of child abuse and child neglect, including the prevention
      of newborn abandonment, the identification of abused and neglected children and the
      provision of necessary ameliorative services to abused and neglected children and
      their families.  The department and each county agency shall conduct an ongoing training and education
      program for local staff, persons required to make reports and other appropriate persons
      in order to familiarize those persons with the reporting and investigative procedures
      for cases of suspected child abuse and the rehabilitative services that are available
      to children and families.  In addition, the department shall, by regulation, establish a program of training
      and certification for persons classified as protective services workers.  The regulations shall provide for the grandfathering of all current permanent protective
      services workers as certified protective services workers.  Upon request by the county agency and approval of the department, the agency may
      conduct the training of the county's protective services workers.

      them from suffering further injury and impairment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6304. Exclusions from child abuse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6304. Exclusions from child abuse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6304. Exclusions from child abuse (2023)
content:
(a) Environmental factors.--No child shall be deemed to be physically or mentally abused based on injuries that
      result solely from environmental factors, such as inadequate housing, furnishings,
      income, clothing and medical care, that are beyond the control of the parent or person
      responsible for the child's welfare with whom the child resides.  This subsection shall not apply to any child-care service as defined in this chapter,
      excluding an adoptive parent.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6316. Admission to private and public hospitals (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Children appearing to suffer any physical or mental condition which may constitute
      child abuse shall be admitted to, treated and maintained in facilities of private
      and public hospitals on the basis of medical need and shall not be refused or deprived
      in any way of proper medical treatment and care.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Subchapter B. Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6312. Persons encouraged to report suspected child abuse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Subchapter B. Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6312. Persons encouraged to report suspected child abuse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6312. Persons encouraged to report suspected child abuse (2023)
content:
Any person may make an oral or written report of suspected child abuse, which may
   be submitted electronically, or cause a report of suspected child abuse to be made
   to the department, county agency or law enforcement, if that person has reasonable
   cause to suspect that a child is a victim of child abuse.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6301. Short title of chapter

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Subchapter B. Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6314. Photographs, medical tests and X-rays of child subject to report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Subchapter B. Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6314. Photographs, medical tests and X-rays of child subject to report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6314. Photographs, medical tests and X-rays of child subject to report (2023)
content:
A person or official required to report cases of suspected child abuse may take or
   cause to be taken photographs of the child who is subject to a report and, if clinically
   indicated, cause to be performed a radiological examination and other medical tests
   on the child.  Medical summaries or reports of the photographs, X-rays and relevant medical tests
   taken shall be sent to the county agency at the time the written report is sent or
   within 48 hours after a report is made by electronic technologies or as soon thereafter
   as possible.  The county agency shall have access to actual photographs or duplicates and X-rays
   and may obtain them or duplicates of them upon request.  Medical summaries or reports of the photographs, X-rays and relevant medical tests
   shall be made available to law enforcement officials in the course of investigating
   cases pursuant to section 6340(a)(9) or (10) (relating to release of information in
   confidential reports).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VII. Abuse of Family›Subchapter B. Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6317. Mandatory reporting and postmortem investigation of deaths
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VII. Abuse of Family › Subchapter B. Provisions and Responsibilities for Reporting Suspected Child Abuse › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6317. Mandatory reporting and postmortem investigation of deaths
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 6317. Mandatory reporting and postmortem investigation of deaths (2023)
content:
A person or official required to report cases of suspected child abuse, including
   employees of a county agency, who has reasonable cause to suspect that a child died
   as a result of child abuse shall report that suspicion to the appropriate coroner
   or medical examiner.  The coroner or medical examiner shall accept the report for investigation and shall
   report his finding to the police, the district attorney, the appropriate county agency
   and, if the report is made by a hospital, the hospital.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7202.1. Duration of personal jurisdiction (2023)
content:
Personal jurisdiction acquired by a tribunal of this State in a proceeding under this
   part or other law of this State relating to a support order continues as long as a
   tribunal of this State has continuing exclusive jurisdiction to modify the tribunal's
   order or continuing jurisdiction to enforce the tribunal's order as provided by sections
   7205 (relating to continuing, exclusive jurisdiction to modify child support orders),
   7206 (relating to continuing jurisdiction to enforce child support orders) and 7211
   (relating to continuing, exclusive jurisdiction to modify spousal support order).

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7210. Application of part to nonresident subject to personal jurisdiction (2023)
content:
A tribunal of this State exercising personal jurisdiction over a nonresident in a
   proceeding under this part, under other law of this State relating to a support order
   or recognizing a foreign support order, may receive evidence from outside this State
   under section 7316 (relating to special rules of evidence and procedure), communicate
   with a tribunal outside this State pursuant to section 7317 (relating to communications
   between tribunals) and obtain discovery through a tribunal outside this State under
   section 7318 (relating to assistance with discovery).  In all other respects, Chapter 71 (relating to general provisions), 72 (relating
   to jurisdiction), 73 (relating to civil provisions of general application), 74 (relating
   to establishment of support order or determination of parentage), 75 (relating to
   enforcement of support order without registration) or 76 (relating to registration,
   enforcement and modification of support order) do not apply, and the tribunal shall
   apply the procedural and substantive law of this State.

content:

content:
(a) Copies of petition.--Upon the filing of a petition authorized by this part, an initiating tribunal of this
      State shall forward three copies of the petition and its accompanying documents:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Subchapter B. Proceedings Involving Two or More States or A Foreign Country›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7204. Simultaneous proceedings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Subchapter B. Proceedings Involving Two or More States or A Foreign Country › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7204. Simultaneous proceedings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7204. Simultaneous proceedings (2023)
content:
(a) Permissible.--A tribunal of this State may exercise jurisdiction to establish a support order if
      the petition or comparable pleading is filed after a petition or comparable pleading
      is filed in another state or a foreign country only if all of the following apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Subchapter C. Reconciliation of Multiple Orders›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7210. Application of part to nonresident subject to personal jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Subchapter C. Reconciliation of Multiple Orders › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7210. Application of part to nonresident subject to personal jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7210. Application of part to nonresident subject to personal jurisdiction (2023)
content:
A tribunal of this State exercising personal jurisdiction over a nonresident in a
   proceeding under this part, under other law of this State relating to a support order
   or recognizing a foreign support order, may receive evidence from outside this State
   under section 7316 (relating to special rules of evidence and procedure), communicate
   with a tribunal outside this State pursuant to section 7317 (relating to communications
   between tribunals) and obtain discovery through a tribunal outside this State under
   section 7318 (relating to assistance with discovery).  In all other respects, Chapter 71 (relating to general provisions), 72 (relating
   to jurisdiction), 73 (relating to civil provisions of general application), 74 (relating
   to establishment of support order or determination of parentage), 75 (relating to
   enforcement of support order without registration) or 76 (relating to registration,
   enforcement and modification of support order) do not apply, and the tribunal shall
   apply the procedural and substantive law of this State.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Inappropriate tribunal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Inappropriate tribunal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Inappropriate tribunal (2023)
content:
If a petition or comparable pleading is received by an inappropriate tribunal of this
   State, it shall forward the pleading and accompanying documents to an appropriate
   tribunal in this State or another state and notify the petitioner where and when the
   pleading was sent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7308. Supervisory duty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7308. Supervisory duty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7308. Supervisory duty (2023)
content:
(a) Secretary.--If the secretary determines that a support enforcement agency is neglecting or refusing
      to provide services to an individual, the secretary may order the agency to perform
      its duties under this part or may provide those services directly to the individual.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Duties of department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Duties of department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7310. Duties of department (2023)
content: (a) Designation.--The department is the State information agency under this part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7316. Special rules of evidence and procedure
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7316. Special rules of evidence and procedure
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7316. Special rules of evidence and procedure (2023)
content:
(a) Physical presence.--The physical presence of a nonresident party who is an individual in a tribunal of
      this State is not required for the establishment, enforcement or modification of a
      support order or the rendition of a judgment determining parentage of a child.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Pleadings and accompanying documents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Pleadings and accompanying documents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7311. Pleadings and accompanying documents (2023)
content:
(a) Verification and content.--In a proceeding under this part, a petitioner seeking to establish a support order
      to determine parentage of a child or to register and modify a support order of a tribunal
      of another state or a foreign country must file a petition.  Unless otherwise ordered under section 7312 (relating to nondisclosure of information
      in exceptional circumstances), the petition or accompanying documents must provide,
      so far as known, the name, residential address and Social Security number of the obligor
      and the obligee or the parent and alleged parent and the name, sex, residential address,
      Social Security number and date of birth of each child for whose benefit support is
      sought or whose parentage is to be determined.  Unless filed at the time of registration, the petition must be accompanied by a
      copy of any support order known to have been issued by another tribunal.  The petition may include any other information that may assist in locating or identifying
      the respondent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7315. Nonparentage as defense
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7315. Nonparentage as defense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7315. Nonparentage as defense (2023)
content:
A party whose parentage of a child has been previously determined by or pursuant to
   law may not plead nonparentage as a defense to a proceeding under this part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7314. Limited immunity of petitioner
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7314. Limited immunity of petitioner
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7314. Limited immunity of petitioner (2023)
content:
(a) Jurisdiction over person.--Participation by a petitioner in a proceeding before a responding tribunal, whether
      in person, by private attorney or through services provided by the support enforcement
      agency, does not confer personal jurisdiction over the petitioner in another proceeding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7317. Communications between tribunals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7317. Communications between tribunals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7317. Communications between tribunals (2023)
content:
A tribunal of this State may communicate with a tribunal outside this State in a record
   or by telephone, e-mail or other means to obtain information concerning the laws;
   the legal effect of a judgment, decree or order of that tribunal;  and the status
   of a proceeding.  A tribunal of this State may furnish similar information by similar means to a tribunal
   outside this State.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7313. Costs and fees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7313. Costs and fees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7313. Costs and fees (2023)
content: (a) Petitioner.--The petitioner may not be required to pay a filing fee or other costs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7312. Nondisclosure of information in exceptional circumstances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7312. Nondisclosure of information in exceptional circumstances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7312. Nondisclosure of information in exceptional circumstances (2023)
content:
If a party alleges in an affidavit or a pleading under oath that the health, safety
   or liberty of a party or child would be jeopardized by disclosure of the specific
   identifying information, the specific identifying information must be sealed and may
   not be disclosed to the other party or the public.  After a hearing in which the tribunal takes into consideration the health, safety
   or liberty of the party or child, the tribunal may order disclosure of information
   that the tribunal determines to be in the interest of justice.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.1. Employer's compliance with income-withholding order of another state
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.1. Employer's compliance with income-withholding order of another state
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.1. Employer's compliance with income-withholding order of another state (2023)
content:
(a) Copy of order.--Upon receipt of an income-withholding order, the obligor's employer shall immediately
      provide a copy of the order to the obligor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 74. Establishment of Support Order or Determination of Parentage›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7401. Establishment of support order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 74. Establishment of Support Order or Determination of Parentage › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7401. Establishment of support order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7401. Establishment of support order (2023)
content:
(a) Jurisdiction.--If a support order entitled to recognition under this part has not been issued, a
      responding tribunal of this State with personal jurisdiction over the parties may
      issue a support order if any of the following apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7318. Assistance with discovery
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7318. Assistance with discovery
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7318. Assistance with discovery (2023)
content: A tribunal of this State may do all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.3. Immunity from civil liability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.3. Immunity from civil liability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.3. Immunity from civil liability (2023)
content:
An employer who complies with an income-withholding order issued in another state
   in accordance with this chapter is not subject to civil liability to an individual
   or agency with regard to the employer's withholding of child support from the obligor's
   income.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Private counsel
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Private counsel
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Private counsel (2023)
content:
An individual may employ private counsel to represent the individual in proceedings
   authorized by this part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 74. Establishment of Support Order or Determination of Parentage›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7402. Proceeding to determine parentage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 74. Establishment of Support Order or Determination of Parentage › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7402. Proceeding to determine parentage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7402. Proceeding to determine parentage (2023)
content:
A tribunal of this State authorized to determine parentage of a child may serve as
   a responding tribunal in a proceeding to determine parentage of a child brought under
   this part or a law or procedure substantially similar to this part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7502. Administrative enforcement of orders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7502. Administrative enforcement of orders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7502. Administrative enforcement of orders (2023)
content:
(a) Initiation.--A party or support enforcement agency seeking to enforce a support order or an income-withholding
      order, or both, issued in another state or a support order issued by a foreign country
      may send the documents required for registering the order to a support enforcement
      agency of this State.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501. Employer's receipt of income-withholding order of another state
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501. Employer's receipt of income-withholding order of another state
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501. Employer's receipt of income-withholding order of another state (2023)
content:
An income-withholding order issued in another state may be sent by or on behalf of
   the obligee, or by the support enforcement agency, to the person or entity defined
   as the obligor's employer under section 4302 (relating to definitions) without first
   filing a petition or comparable pleading or registering the order with a tribunal
   of this State.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.2. Compliance with multiple income-withholding orders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.2. Compliance with multiple income-withholding orders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.2. Compliance with multiple income-withholding orders (2023)
content:
If an obligor's employer receives multiple income-withholding orders with respect
   to the earnings of the same obligor, the employer satisfies the terms of the multiple
   orders if the employer complies with the law of the state of the obligor's principal
   place of employment to establish the priorities for withholding and allocating income
   withheld for multiple child-support obligees.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.5. Contest by obligor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.5. Contest by obligor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.5. Contest by obligor (2023)
content:
An obligor may contest the validity or enforcement of an income-withholding order
   issued in another state and received directly by an employer in this State by registering
   the order in a tribunal of this State and filing a contest to that order as provided
   in Chapter 76 (relating to registration, enforcement and modification of support order)
   or otherwise contesting the order in the same manner as if the order had been issued
   by a tribunal of this State.  The obligor shall give notice of the contest to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7319. Receipt and disbursement of payments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 73. Civil Provisions of General Application › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7319. Receipt and disbursement of payments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7319. Receipt and disbursement of payments (2023)
content:
(a) Payments.--A support enforcement agency or tribunal of this State shall disburse promptly any
      amounts received pursuant to a support order, as directed by the order.  The agency or tribunal shall furnish to a requesting party or tribunal outside this
      State or of a foreign country a certified statement by the custodian of the record
      of the amounts and dates of all payments received.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.4. Penalties for noncompliance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 75. Enforcement of Support Order Without Registration › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.4. Penalties for noncompliance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7501.4. Penalties for noncompliance (2023)
content:
An employer that willfully fails to comply with an income-withholding order issued
   in another state and received for enforcement is subject to the same penalties that
   may be imposed for noncompliance with an order issued by a tribunal of this State.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 76. Registration, Enforcement and Modification of Support Order›Subchapter A. Registration for Enforcement of Support Order›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7601. Registration of order for enforcement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 76. Registration, Enforcement and Modification of Support Order › Subchapter A. Registration for Enforcement of Support Order › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7601. Registration of order for enforcement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7601. Registration of order for enforcement (2023)
content:
A support order or an income-withholding order issued in another state or a foreign
   support order may be registered in this State for enforcement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations›Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support›Chapter 76. Registration, Enforcement and Modification of Support Order›Subchapter A. Registration for Enforcement of Support Order›PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7604. Choice of law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 23 Pa.C.S.A. Domestic Relations › Part VIII. Uniform Interstate Family Support › Chapter 76. Registration, Enforcement and Modification of Support Order › Subchapter A. Registration for Enforcement of Support Order › PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7604. Choice of law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 23 Pa.C.S.A. § 7604. Choice of law (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject to subsection (d), the law of the issuing state or foreign country governs
      the following:
